• Glutamine:phosphoribosylpyrophosphate (PRPP) amidotransferase.
• Inhibited by: AMP and GMP.
• Activated by: PRPP (feed-forward).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 5-year-old boy presents with cognitive deficits, signs of gouty arthritis, and a history of self-mutilation (biting lips and fingers). Identify the underlying enzyme deficiency.
back:
• Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT).
• Leads to: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
• Result: Excessive uric acid production and failed purine salvage.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP) as a feed-forward activator in purine metabolism.
back:
• PRPP concentration is usually low (below Km).
• Small increases in PRPP levels proportionally increase the rate of the amidotransferase reaction.
• Ensures synthesis matches substrate availability.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the mechanism of action between Allopurinol and Probenecid in the clinical management of hyperuricemia.
back:
• Allopurinol: Structural analog of hypoxanthine; inhibits Xanthine Oxidase to reduce uric acid production.
• Probenecid: Uricosuric agent; inhibits renal tubular reabsorption to increase uric acid excretion.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the energy source (nucleoside triphosphate) specifically required for the conversion of Inosine Monophosphate (IMP) to Adenosine Monophosphate (AMP).
back:
• Guanosine triphosphate (GTP).
• Note: Conversion of IMP to GMP requires ATP.
• This reciprocal energy use balances adenine and guanine pools.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: During purine degradation, both hypoxanthine and guanine are converted into the common nitrogenous intermediate [___] before becoming uric acid.
back:
• Xanthine.
• Hypoxanthine is oxidized by Xanthine Oxidase.
• Guanine is deaminated by Guanase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient undergoing chemotherapy for leukemia develops sudden-onset joint pain and hyperuricemia. Explain the biochemical basis of this finding.
back:
• Tumor Lysis Syndrome.
• High cell turnover causes massive nucleic acid breakdown.
• Excessive purine degradation leads to overproduction of uric acid.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe why HGPRT deficiency in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome causes a massive increase in de novo purine synthesis.
back:
• Reduced salvage increases PRPP levels (substrate availability).
• Reduced IMP/GMP levels remove feedback inhibition on the de novo pathway.
• Dual effect over-activates PRPP amidotransferase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish between the donors of nitrogen versus carbon in the construction of the purine ring.
back:
• Nitrogen Donors: Aspartate, Glycine, and Glutamine.
• Carbon Donors: Glycine, CO2, and N10-formyltetrahydrofolate.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the parent purine nucleotide that serves as the immediate precursor for both AMP and GMP.
back:
• Inosine Monophosphate (IMP).
• Base: Hypoxanthine.
• Formed after a 10-step de novo pathway from PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The committed and rate-limiting step of de-novo purine synthesis is catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back: Glutamine:PRPP amidotransferase. • Inhibited by AMP and GMP (feedback inhibition). • Feed-forward activated by PRPP substrate levels.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 5-year-old boy presents with cognitive impairment, hyperuricemia, and self-mutilating behavior (biting lips/fingers). Name the deficient enzyme in the salvage pathway.
back: Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT). • Diagnosis: Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome. • Causes failure to salvage hypoxanthine/guanine and excess de-novo purine production.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of PRPP (5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate) in the regulation and initiation of the de-novo purine pathway.
back: • Acts as the 'activated pentose' donor of ribose 5-phosphate. • Its intracellular concentration is normally low (below Km), making it a key rate-governing substrate.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the pharmacological targets of Mycophenolic acid and Allopurinol in purine metabolism.
back: • Mycophenolic acid: Reversible inhibitor of IMP dehydrogenase (blocks GMP synthesis in T/B cells). • Allopurinol: Inhibits Xanthine Oxidase (blocks uric acid production).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Molecular sources of the purine ring
front: Identify the specific amino acid precursors that contribute nitrogen atoms N1, N3, and N9 to the purine ring structure.
back: • N1: Aspartate. • N3 and N9: Glutamine (amide nitrogen). • Glycine contributes N7.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The 'parent' purine nucleotide formed as the first complete purine ring structure in the de-novo pathway is [___].
back: Inosine Monophosphate (IMP). • Contains the base Hypoxanthine. • Serves as the branch point for AMP and GMP synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A child with Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID) shows lymphocytopenia and high dATP levels. Explain the metabolic mechanism causing cell death.
back: Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency. • Accumulated dATP inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase. • This prevents DNA synthesis/proliferation in T and B cells.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Reciprocal energy requirement in purine synthesis
front: Describe the cross-regulation between AMP and GMP synthesis regarding their energy requirements (GTP and ATP).
back: • AMP synthesis from IMP requires GTP. • GMP synthesis from IMP requires ATP. • This ensures balanced production of both purine nucleotides.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish the metabolic roles of Adenine Phosphoribosyltransferase (APRT) from HGPRT.
back: • APRT: Salvages Adenine + PRPP into AMP. • HGPRT: Salvages Hypoxanthine into IMP and Guanine into GMP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the common end product of both dietary and endogenous purine degradation in humans.
back: Uric Acid. • Formed via Xanthine and Hypoxanthine oxidation. • Excreted in urine; excessive levels cause Gout.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The committed step of de novo purine synthesis, which is inhibited by AMP and GMP, is catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back:
• Glutamine:phosphoribosylpyrophosphate (PRPP) amidotransferase
• Replaces PRPP pyrophosphate with glutamine amide group
• Highly regulated by end-product feedback.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 4-year-old male presents with orange sand-like crystals in his diaper and compulsive biting of his lips and fingers. Identify the enzyme deficiency.
back:
• HGPRT (Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase)
• Condition: Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome (X-linked recessive)
• Leads to failure of purine salvage and hyperuricemia.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of PRPP (5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate) in both de novo and salvage purine pathways.
back:
• De novo: Acts as the ribose 5-phosphate donor and allosteric activator
• Salvage: Provides the ribose-phosphate moiety for free bases
• Concentration directly regulates the rate of purine synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the pharmacological mechanisms of Allopurinol versus Probenecid in treating chronic gout.
back:
• Allopurinol: Xanthine Oxidase inhibitor; decreases uric acid production
• Probenecid: Uricosuric agent; increases renal excretion of uric acid
• Choice depends on 'overproducer' vs 'underexcretor' status.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the specific nucleoside triphosphate required as an energy source to convert IMP into Adenosine Monophosphate (AMP).
back:
• GTP (Guanosine Triphosphate)
• Note: Conversion of IMP to GMP requires ATP
• This cross-regulation ensures balanced purine pools.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Intracellular accumulation of dATP in Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency causes immune dysfunction by inhibiting the enzyme [___].
back:
• Ribonucleotide reductase
• Prevents synthesis of all deoxyribonucleotides
• Results in Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient on chemotherapy develops joint pain and swelling. Analysis shows needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals. Why does cell turnover cause this?
back:
• Rapid cell death increases nucleic acid degradation
• Excessive purines are catabolized to uric acid
• Leads to secondary hyperuricemia and acute gouty arthritis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the mechanism by which Methotrexate interferes with de novo purine synthesis in rapidly dividing cancer cells.
back:
• Inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR)
• Depletes Tetrahydrofolate (THF) stores
• THF is required as a carbon donor (formyl groups) for purine ring construction.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish between the final degradative products of purines in humans versus other mammals.
back:
• Humans: Uric acid (insoluble; excreted in urine)
• Other Mammals: Allantoin (soluble; produced via urate oxidase)
• Absence of urate oxidase in humans predisposes to gout.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: List the three amino acids that serve as essential precursors providing atoms for the purine ring structure.
back:
• Glycine (provides carbons and nitrogen)
• Glutamine (provides amide nitrogens)
• Aspartic Acid (provides nitrogen).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The committed and rate-limiting step of de-novo purine synthesis is catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back:
* **Glutamine-phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate (PRPP) amidotransferase**.
* Inhibited by AMP and GMP (feedback inhibition).
* Activated by the concentration of PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 2-year-old boy presents with cognitive delay, spasticity, and compulsive biting of his lips and fingers. Laboratory tests reveal hyperuricemia. This condition results from a deficiency of [___].
back:
* **HGPRT** (Hypoxanthine-Guanine Phosphoribosyltransferase).
* Diagnosis: **Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome**.
* Pathophysiology: Failure of the purine salvage pathway leads to excessive de-novo synthesis and uric acid production.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of cross-regulation regarding energy sources in the conversion of Inosine Monophosphate (IMP) to AMP and GMP.
back:
* **AMP synthesis** requires **GTP** as the energy source.
* **GMP synthesis** requires **ATP** as the energy source.
* Benefit: Ensures a balanced production of adenine and guanine nucleotides based on cellular energy levels.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the starting substrates used in the de-novo purine synthesis pathway versus those utilized in the purine salvage pathway.
back:
* **De-novo:** Builds the ring using **PRPP**, amino acids (**Glycine, Glutamine, Aspartate**), $CO_2$, and Formyl-THF.
* **Salvage:** Recycles **free purine bases** (Adenine, Guanine, Hypoxanthine) by reattaching them to **PRPP**.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the enzyme targeted by the drug Mycophenolic acid and its specific clinical application in immunology.
back:
* Enzyme: **IMP Dehydrogenase**.
* Application: **Immunosuppressant** used to prevent graft rejection.
* Mechanism: Deprives proliferating T and B cells of necessary GMP for nucleic acid synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In the construction of the purine ring, the nitrogen atoms at positions 3 and 9 are donated by [___].
back:
* **Glutamine** (specifically the amide group).
* Note: Other donors include Aspartate (N1) and Glycine (C4, C5, N7).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient with leukemia undergoing aggressive chemotherapy suddenly develops excruciating pain in the big toe. Explain the biochemical mechanism for this presentation.
back:
* **Secondary Gout**.
* Mechanism: Massive cell lysis releases nucleic acids; purine degradation increases uric acid levels.
* Final step: **Xanthine Oxidase** converts xanthine to insoluble uric acid crystals.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe how a deficiency in Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) leads to the depletion of T and B cells (SCID).
back:
* **Adenosine/dATP** accumulates in lymphocytes.
* Elevated dATP inhibits **Ribonucleotide Reductase**.
* This prevents the production of all deoxyribonucleotides, halting DNA synthesis and cell division.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the mechanisms of Allopurinol and Probenecid in managing hyperuricemia.
back:
* **Allopurinol:** Inhibits **Xanthine Oxidase**, reducing the production of uric acid.
* **Probenecid:** A **uricosuric agent** that inhibits renal reabsorption of uric acid, increasing urinary excretion.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the specific 'parent' nucleotide that is the first complete purine synthesized in the de-novo pathway.
back:
* **Inosine Monophosphate (IMP)**.
* Contains the base **Hypoxanthine**.
* Serves as the branch point for both AMP and GMP synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The specific amino acid that provides the most atoms (C4, C5, and N7) to the purine ring structure during de-novo synthesis is [___].
back:
• Glycine
• Provides the central carbon-nitrogen backbone
• Entire molecule is incorporated into the ring

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 2-year-old boy presents with intellectual disability, gouty arthritis, and compulsive biting of his lips and fingers. This clinical picture suggests a deficiency of [___].
back:
• Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT)
• Diagnosis: Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome
• Leads to decreased purine salvage and excessive uric acid production

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of intracellular PRPP concentration in regulating the committed step of de-novo purine synthesis.
back:
• Acts as a potent feed-forward activator
• Stimulates Glutamine:PRPP amidotransferase (GPAT)
• Intracellular levels are usually below Km, making the rate highly sensitive to PRPP availability

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the nitrogen donors and energy sources used in the conversion of IMP to AMP versus IMP to GMP.
back:
• AMP synthesis: Requires Aspartate (nitrogen) and GTP (energy source)
• GMP synthesis: Requires Glutamine (nitrogen) and ATP (energy source)
• This reciprocal regulation ensures balanced nucleotide pools

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: State the mechanism by which Mycophenolic acid acts as an immunosuppressant to prevent graft rejection.
back:
• Reversibly inhibits IMP Dehydrogenase
• Deprives T and B cells of GMP/GTP
• Halts nucleic acid synthesis in rapidly proliferating immune cells

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In the final step of purine catabolism in humans, the enzyme [___] oxidizes xanthine into uric acid.
back:
• Xanthine Oxidase
• Final product: Uric Acid
• Target of the drug Allopurinol

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A child presents with Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID) due to Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency. Why does this enzyme lack inhibit DNA synthesis?
back:
• Causes accumulation of dATP
• dATP allosterically inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase
• Prevents the formation of all deoxyribonucleotides (dNTPs) required for replication

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe how Allopurinol reduces the overall 'de-novo' purine synthesis rate in patients with intact salvage enzymes.
back:
• Salvaged hypoxanthine (not oxidized to urate) consumes PRPP
• Allopurinol metabolite (Oxypurinol) also consumes PRPP
• Depleted PRPP levels reduce the activity of the rate-limiting amidotransferase

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish between the starting materials used in the de-novo pathway versus the salvage pathway of purine synthesis.
back:
• De-novo: Uses simple precursors like amino acids (Glutamine, Glycine), CO2, and PRPP
• Salvage: Uses preformed free bases (Adenine, Guanine, Hypoxanthine) and PRPP
• Salvage is energetically more efficient

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the primary allosteric activator and the group of inhibitors for the enzyme PRPP Synthetase.
back:
• Activator: Inorganic Phosphate (Pi)
• Inhibitors: Purine ribonucleotides (AMP, GMP, IMP)
• Operates via end-product feedback inhibition

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The committed step of de novo purine synthesis is catalyzed by [___], which is allosterically inhibited by the end-products AMP and GMP.
back:
• Glutamine:phosphoribosylpyrophosphate (PRPP) amidotransferase.
• Converts PRPP to 5-phosphoribosylamine.
• Requires glutamine as a nitrogen donor.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 2-year-old boy presents with cognitive impairment and a history of biting his lips and fingertips. Lab results show severe hyperuricemia. Name the deficient enzyme.
back:
• HGPRT (Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase).
• Diagnosis: Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome.
• Result: Failure of purine salvage and increased de novo synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which methotrexate inhibits purine nucleotide synthesis during chemotherapy.
back:
• Inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR).
• Depletes Tetrahydrofolate (THF) pools.
• Blocks carbon donation from N10-formyl-THF required for purine ring closure.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the metabolic impact of HGPRT deficiency versus PRPP Synthetase overactivity on intracellular PRPP levels.
back:
• HGPRT deficiency: Increases PRPP levels due to decreased consumption in salvage.
• PRPP Synthetase overactivity: Directly increases PRPP production.
• Both: Accelerate de novo synthesis leading to gout.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the specific enzymatic reaction inhibited by Mycophenolic acid to prevent graft rejection in transplant patients.
back:
• Inosine Monophosphate (IMP) Dehydrogenase.
• Blocks conversion of IMP to GMP.
• Prevents proliferation of T and B cells by depriving them of guanine nucleotides.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In the degradation of purines, the enzyme [___] converts both hypoxanthine and xanthine into the final excretory product, uric acid.
back:
• Xanthine Oxidase.
• Inhibited by Allopurinol.
• Produces H2O2 as a byproduct in the liver and small intestine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient with Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID) lacks Adenosine Deaminase (ADA). Explain why this deficiency causes lymphotoxicity.
back:
• Accumulation of dATP.
• High dATP inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase.
• Depletion of dNTPs prevents DNA synthesis and cell division in lymphocytes.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the metabolic fate of dietary purines in the human body according to clinical biochemistry standards.
back:
• Minimally utilized for tissue nucleic acid synthesis.
• Majority degraded in intestinal mucosal cells.
• Converted to uric acid and excreted in urine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the roles of Thioredoxin and NADPH in the reduction of ribonucleotides to deoxyribonucleotides.
back:
• Thioredoxin: Acts as the immediate hydrogen donor for Ribonucleotide Reductase.
• NADPH: Provides reducing equivalents to regenerate reduced Thioredoxin via Thioredoxin Reductase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: List the three essential amino acids that serve as precursors for the de novo synthesis of the purine ring.
back:
• Glycine (provides carbons and nitrogen).
• Aspartate (provides nitrogen).
• Glutamine (provides nitrogen).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The committed and rate-limiting step of de novo purine synthesis is catalyzed by [___], which is feedback inhibited by AMP and GMP.
back:
• Glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase
• Activated by high levels of PRPP
• Inhibited by the end-products AMP and GMP

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 3-year-old male presents with cognitive impairment, orange 'sand' in his diaper, and a habit of biting his own lips. This condition results from a deficiency in [___].
back:
• HGPRT (Hypoxanthine-Guanine Phosphoribosyltransferase)
• Diagnosis: Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome
• Leads to inability to salvage hypoxanthine/guanine

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of N10-formyl-tetrahydrofolate in the de novo construction of the purine ring.
back:
• Acts as a one-carbon donor
• Specifically contributes carbon atoms at positions C2 and C8
• Inhibition of this step by methotrexate halts DNA replication

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the energy sources required for the conversion of Inosine Monophosphate (IMP) to AMP versus its conversion to GMP.
back:
• IMP to AMP: Requires GTP as energy source
• IMP to GMP: Requires ATP as energy source
• This cross-regulation ensures a balance of adenine and guanine

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the mechanism by which Mycophenolic acid acts as an immunosuppressant in transplant patients.
back:
• Reversible inhibitor of IMP dehydrogenase
• Deprives rapidly proliferating T and B cells of GMP
• Prevents graft rejection by limiting lymphocyte proliferation

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The enzyme [___] is responsible for converting hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to the final excretory product, uric acid.
back:
• Xanthine Oxidase
• Targeted by the drug Allopurinol
• Produces hydrogen peroxide as a byproduct

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: An infant with recurrent infections is diagnosed with Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency. How does this deficiency cause lymphotoxicity?
back:
• Adenosine/dATP accumulates
• dATP inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase
• This prevents DNA synthesis, leading to Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID)

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Cross-talk between Salvage and De Novo Pathways
front: Why does HGPRT deficiency (Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome) cause a massive increase in de novo purine synthesis rather than just a decrease in salvage?
back:
• Excess PRPP (not used in salvage) activates the rate-limiting amidotransferase
• Reduced IMP/GMP levels remove feedback inhibition from the de novo pathway

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish between the final degradation products of purines in humans versus most other mammals.
back:
• Humans: Uric acid (insoluble; lack urate oxidase)
• Other Mammals: Allantoin (soluble; converted by urate oxidase)
• Humans are prone to Gout due to this lack

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: List the three specific amino acids required to provide nitrogen and carbon atoms for the de novo synthesis of the purine ring.
back:
• Glycine (provides C4, C5, N7)
• Glutamine (provides N3, N9)
• Aspartate (provides N1)

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: PRPP as a universal nucleotide precursor
front: The activated pentose that serves as the essential ribose 5-phosphate donor for both de-novo and salvage purine synthesis is [___].
back:
• 5-Phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP).
• Synthesized from Ribose 5-phosphate and ATP.
• Catalyzed by PRPP synthetase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 2-year-old boy presents with cognitive impairment and a compulsive history of biting his lips and fingers. Laboratory tests show significant hyperuricemia. Name the deficient enzyme.
back:
• HGPRT (Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase).
• Condition: Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome.
• Results in failed purine salvage and excessive uric acid production.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain how intracellular levels of PRPP and purine nucleotides (AMP/GMP) coordinately regulate the activity of Glutamine:PRPP amidotransferase.
back:
• PRPP acts as a feed-forward activator.
• AMP and GMP act as feed-back inhibitors.
• This is the committed step of de-novo purine synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the energy requirements and substrate sources between the de-novo purine pathway and the salvage pathway.
back:
• De-novo: Energy-expensive (multiple ATP); uses amino acids (Asp, Gly, Gln) and CO2.
• Salvage: Energy-efficient; recycles preformed bases (Adenine, Guanine, Hypoxanthine) using only PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the pharmacological mechanism of Mycophenolic acid in preventing graft rejection.
back:
• Reversibly inhibits IMP dehydrogenase.
• Deprives T and B cells of GMP.
• Halts lymphocyte proliferation, reducing immune response.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In the purine ring, the nitrogen at position 1 is donated by [___], while the nitrogen at position 9 is donated by [___].
back:
• Aspartate (N1).
• Glutamine (N9).
• Note: Glycine provides C4, C5, and N7.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient with acute podagra and needle-shaped negative birefringent crystals is started on Allopurinol. This drug works by inhibiting [___].
back:
• Xanthine Oxidase.
• Prevents conversion of hypoxanthine and xanthine into uric acid.
• Facilitates excretion of more soluble precursors.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Detail the mechanism by which Ribonucleotide Reductase is regenerated to continue the conversion of ribonucleotides to deoxyribonucleotides.
back:
• Uses Thioredoxin as a hydrogen donor (forming a disulfide bond).
• Thioredoxin is regenerated by Thioredoxin Reductase.
• Requires NADPH as the ultimate reducing power.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish the specific energy sources required to convert Inosine Monophosphate (IMP) into AMP versus GMP.
back:
• AMP synthesis requires GTP.
• GMP synthesis requires ATP.
• This cross-regulation ensures balanced production of both purine types.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the final, relatively insoluble excretory product of purine catabolism in humans and the enzyme responsible for its final two oxidative steps.
back:
• Product: Uric Acid.
• Enzyme: Xanthine Oxidase.
• Humans lack Urate Oxidase, which would convert it to more soluble Allantoin.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The committed step of de novo purine synthesis, which is inhibited by the end-products AMP and GMP, is catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back: - Glutamine:phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate (PRPP) amidotransferase. - This enzyme replaces the pyrophosphate group of PRPP with an amide nitrogen from glutamine. - It is the primary rate-limiting and regulatory point of the pathway.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A male infant presents with developmental delay, orange 'sand-like' crystals in his diaper, and a history of biting his own lips and fingers. Name the deficient enzyme.
back: - Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT). - This results in Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome. - Pathophysiology involves a failure of the purine salvage pathway, leading to excessive uric acid production and hyperuricemia.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of N10-formyl tetrahydrofolate in purine synthesis and how its clinical inhibition differs between humans and bacteria.
back: - Provides Carbon 2 and Carbon 8 to the purine ring. - Methotrexate inhibits human purine synthesis by blocking dihydrofolate reductase. - Sulfonamides inhibit bacterial folic acid synthesis; humans remain unaffected as they rely on dietary folate.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the biochemical targets and clinical indications for Mycophenolic acid versus Allopurinol in purine metabolism.
back: - Mycophenolic acid: Inhibits IMP dehydrogenase to block GMP synthesis; used as an immunosuppressant for transplants. - Allopurinol: Inhibits Xanthine Oxidase to block uric acid production; used to treat gout and prevent hyperuricemia.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the specific enzymatic step and the energy source (nucleotide) required for the synthesis of AMP from the parent molecule IMP.
back: - Enzyme: Adenylosuccinate synthetase. - Energy Source: Guanosine Triphosphate (GTP). - This requirement for GTP ensures balanced production between adenine and guanine nucleotides via reciprocal energy utilization.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The clinical finding of severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) associated with an accumulation of dATP and subsequent inhibition of ribonucleotide reductase is diagnostic for [___].
back: - Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency. - Accumulated dATP acts as a potent allosteric inhibitor of ribonucleotide reductase. - This prevents the production of all deoxyribonucleotides, resulting in the failure of T and B cell proliferation.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient undergoing chemotherapy for leukemia suddenly develops severe joint pain and high serum uric acid. Describe the underlying metabolic cause.
back: - Tumor Lysis Syndrome. - Massive cell death leads to the release and degradation of nucleic acids. - The resulting overload of purine bases is catabolized into uric acid, leading to secondary hyperuricemia and acute gouty arthritis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism why HGPRT deficiency leads to a massive increase in de novo purine synthesis rather than just a loss of recycling.
back: - Loss of salvage leads to the accumulation of PRPP (a substrate activator). - Depletion of IMP and GMP removes the feedback inhibition on the amidotransferase enzyme. - This combination hyper-activates the de novo pathway, causing uric acid overproduction.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish between the energetic efficiency of the de novo pathway and the salvage pathway for purine production.
back: - De novo: Requires significant energy (ATP) and multiple amino acids to build the ring. - Salvage: Energetically 'cheap' as it utilizes preformed bases and a single PRPP molecule. - Most tissues prioritize salvage to conserve energy.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the molybdenum-containing enzyme that serves as the final common pathway for the degradation of both hypoxanthine and guanine into uric acid.
back: - Xanthine Oxidase. - It converts hypoxanthine to xanthine, and xanthine to uric acid. - It is the primary target for allopurinol and febuxostat in the management of chronic gout.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The committed and rate-limiting step of de novo purine synthesis is catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back:
• Glutamine:phosphoribosylpyrophosphate (PRPP) amidotransferase.
• Inhibited by: AMP, GMP, and IMP.
• Activated by: PRPP concentration.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 2-year-old boy presents with self-mutilation behavior and orange sand-like crystals in his diaper. Identify the defective enzyme and the salvaged base that cannot be reused.
back:
• Enzyme: Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT).
• Bases: Hypoxanthine and Guanine.
• Condition: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of PRPP Synthetase in purine metabolism and its regulation by inorganic phosphate.
back:
• Function: Converts Ribose 5-phosphate to PRPP using ATP.
• Activator: Inorganic phosphate (Pi).
• Inhibitor: Purine ribonucleotides (end-product inhibition).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the impact of HGPRT deficiency on the de novo purine pathway versus the salvage pathway regarding PRPP levels.
back:
• Salvage: Decreased (failure to consume PRPP).
• De Novo: Increased (excess PRPP stimulates amidotransferase).
• Result: Massive overproduction and degradation of purines.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the specific enzyme inhibited by Mycophenolic acid to prevent graft rejection in transplant patients.
back:
• Enzyme: IMP Dehydrogenase.
• Mechanism: Prevents conversion of IMP to GMP.
• Effect: Deprives proliferating T and B cells of necessary nucleic acids.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In the diagnosis of Gout, joint fluid aspiration under polarized light microscopy typically reveals negatively birefringent [___] shaped crystals.
back:
• Needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals.
• Found within polymorphonuclear leukocytes.
• Essential for definitive diagnosis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient with hyperuricemia is treated with Allopurinol. Apply your knowledge of purine degradation to explain how this drug reduces uric acid production.
back:
• Mechanism: Reversible inhibitor of Xanthine Oxidase.
• Step: Blocks Hypoxanthine → Xanthine → Uric Acid.
• Benefit: Accumulation of more soluble hypoxanthine/xanthine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain how a deficiency in Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) leads to the failure of lymphocyte proliferation in SCID.
back:
• Mechanism: Accumulation of dATP.
• Effect: Inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase.
• Consequence: Depletes deoxyribonucleotides (dNTPs), halting DNA synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish between the roles of Glutamine and Aspartate in the construction of the purine ring.
back:
• Glutamine: Donates N3 and N9 atoms.
• Aspartate: Donates N1 atom.
• Both: Essential nitrogen donors for de novo synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the parent purine nucleotide from which both Adenosine Monophosphate (AMP) and Guanosine Monophosphate (GMP) are derived.
back:
• Inosine Monophosphate (IMP).
• IMP contains the base Hypoxanthine.
• Serves as the branch point for adenine and guanine synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting step in de novo pyrimidine synthesis is catalyzed by the cytosolic enzyme [___].
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
• Inhibited allosterically by UTP.
• Activated allosterically by PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia and growth retardation. Lab tests reveal excessive orotic acid in the urine. This condition is caused by a deficiency in [___].
back:
• UMP Synthase (Hereditary Orotic Aciduria).
• Involves orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase domains.
• Leads to inability to synthesize pyrimidines.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP) in the regulation of the pyrimidine biosynthetic pathway.
back:
• Acts as an essential allosteric activator of CPS II.
• Serves as the donor of the ribose 5-phosphate group.
• Couples the availability of the pentose sugar to the rate of ring synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: CPS I vs CPS II Distinction
front: Differentiate between Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and II (CPS II) regarding their nitrogen source and cellular location.
back:
• CPS I: Uses Ammonia (NH3); located in Mitochondria (Urea Cycle).
• CPS II: Uses Glutamine (gamma-amide group); located in Cytosol (Pyrimidine Synthesis).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the specific enzyme inhibited by the anticancer drug 5-Fluorouracil and describe the metabolic block it creates.
back:
• Enzyme: Thymidylate Synthase.
• Block: Prevents conversion of dUMP to dTMP.
• Result: Starves the cell of thymidine, arresting DNA replication.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: While most enzymes of pyrimidine synthesis are cytosolic, the enzyme [___] is uniquely associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane.
back:
• Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase.
• Catalyzes the oxidation of dihydroorotate to orotic acid.
• This is the only mitochondrial step in the pathway.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Orotic aciduria in Urea Cycle defects
front: A patient presents with high urinary orotic acid but also exhibits hyperammonemia. Identify the underlying enzyme defect and explain why orotic acid is elevated.
back:
• Diagnosis: Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency.
• Mechanism: Mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate accumulates and leaks into the cytosol.
• Overwhelms CPS II and floods the pyrimidine pathway.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the biochemical basis for using Uridine to treat hereditary orotic aciduria.
back:
• Uridine is salvaged by nucleoside kinases to UMP.
• Bypasses the metabolic block at UMP Synthase.
• UTP formed via salvage feedback-inhibits CPS II, reducing orotic acid production.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the solubility and end products of pyrimidine degradation with those of purine degradation in humans.
back:
• Pyrimidines: Products are highly soluble (beta-alanine, beta-aminoisobutyrate, NH3, CO2).
• Purines: Product is Uric Acid, which is relatively insoluble and can precipitate (Gout).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Molecular sources of the pyrimidine ring
front: Identify the atoms contributed by Glutamine and Aspartate to the pyrimidine ring structure.
back:
• Glutamine: Contributes the Amide Nitrogen (N3).
• Aspartate: Contributes C4, C5, C6, and Nitrogen (N1).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting enzyme of cytosolic de novo pyrimidine synthesis, which is activated by PRPP and inhibited by UTP, is [___].
back:
Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).

*   Utilizes glutamine, CO2, and 2 ATP.
*   Occurs in the cytosol (unlike CPS I in mitochondria).
*   Part of the multifunctional CAD enzyme complex.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A child presents with physical retardation and megaloblastic anemia unresponsive to B12/folate. Lab results show high urinary orotic acid. Identify the enzyme deficiency.
back:
UMP Synthase (Hereditary Orotic Aciduria).

*   Defective conversion of orotic acid to UMP.
*   Treatment: Oral Uridine (bypasses the block via salvage pathway).
*   Characterized by macrocytic anemia and normal ammonia levels.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain how 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) interrupts pyrimidine synthesis to achieve an antineoplastic effect.
back:
It is metabolized to 5-FdUMP, acting as a 'suicide inhibitor' of Thymidylate Synthase.

*   Permanently binds the enzyme.
*   Blocks dUMP to dTMP conversion.
*   Deprives cells of thymidine required for DNA replication.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the diagnostic markers of Orotic Aciduria caused by UMP Synthase deficiency versus Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency.
back:
*   OTC Deficiency: High ammonia (hyperammonemia) and decreased BUN.
*   UMP Synthase Deficiency: Normal ammonia and megaloblastic anemia.
*   Commonality: Both show high urinary orotic acid due to carbamoyl phosphate spillover.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the unique role of N5, N10-methylene tetrahydrofolate in the conversion of dUMP to dTMP.
back:
It acts as both a carbon donor and a reducing agent.

*   Provides a methyl group to the pyrimidine ring.
*   Is oxidized to Dihydrofolate (DHF) during the reaction.
*   Requires Dihydrofolate Reductase for regeneration.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Unlike other enzymes of the de novo pyrimidine pathway which are cytosolic, Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase is located in the [___].
back:
Inner Mitochondrial Membrane.

*   Converts dihydroorotate to orotic acid (orotate).
*   Linked to the electron transport chain (FAD-dependent).
*   Essential for completing the first pyrimidine ring structure.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A cancer patient on Methotrexate develops myelosuppression. Describe the biochemical reason for the resulting deficiency in thymidine monophosphate (dTMP).
back:
Methotrexate inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR).

*   Prevents regeneration of Tetrahydrofolate (THF).
*   Depletes N5, N10-methylene THF levels.
*   Indirectly stalls dTMP synthesis by starving Thymidylate Synthase of its methyl donor.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the logic behind using Uridine to treat UMP Synthase deficiency (Hereditary Orotic Aciduria).
back:
Uridine is salvaged by Uridine Kinase into UMP.

*   Bypasses the enzymatic block at orotate phosphoribosyltransferase.
*   Provides the necessary pyrimidines for RNA/DNA synthesis.
*   Inhibits CPS II (via UTP feedback), reducing further orotic acid production.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the solubility and end products of human purine versus pyrimidine degradation.
back:
*   Purines: Uric acid; relatively insoluble; can cause gout/stones.
*   Pyrimidines: Beta-alanine and Beta-aminoisobutyrate; highly soluble.
*   Both produce ammonia (NH3) and CO2 as metabolic byproducts.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Role of PRPP in nucleotide synthesis
front: Name the activated pentose sugar required to donate ribose-5-phosphate for both the de novo and salvage pathways of pyrimidine synthesis.
back:
5-Phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP).

*   Synthesized from Ribose-5-phosphate and ATP.
*   Enzyme: PRPP Synthetase.
*   Acts as an essential scaffold for the pyrimidine ring attachment.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting step in human de-novo pyrimidine synthesis is regulated by the cytosolic enzyme [___].
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II)
• Inhibited by UTP (end-product)
• Activated by PRPP

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A child presents with megaloblastic anemia and excessive urinary orotic acid. Symptoms do not resolve with Vitamin B12 or Folate. Identify the most likely enzymatic defect.
back:
• UMP Synthase deficiency (Hereditary Orotic Aciduria)
• Affects orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase domains
• Treated with oral Uridine

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of the CAD complex during the initial stages of pyrimidine biosynthesis.
back:
• Multi-functional cytosolic polypeptide
• Contains CPS II, Aspartate transcarbamoylase, and Dihydroorotase
• Catalyzes the first three steps from Glutamine to Dihydroorotate

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the orotic aciduria found in UMP Synthase deficiency with that seen in Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency.
back:
• UMP Synthase: Normal ammonia levels, megaloblastic anemia present
• OTC Deficiency: Elevated blood ammonia (hyperammonemia), urea cycle defect, no megaloblastic anemia

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the specific biochemical mechanism by which 5-Fluorouracil acts as an antineoplastic agent.
back:
• Converted to 5-FdUMP
• Acts as a suicide inhibitor of Thymidylate Synthase
• Halts conversion of dUMP to dTMP, blocking DNA synthesis

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Unlike purine catabolism which ends in uric acid, pyrimidine ring degradation results in the highly soluble product [___].
back:
• Beta-alanine (from Uracil/Cytosine)
• Beta-aminoisobutyrate (from Thymine)
• Released with CO2 and NH3

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A cancer patient on Methotrexate develops impaired cell division. Describe the specific impact of this drug on pyrimidine-specific metabolism.
back:
• Inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR)
• Depletes Tetrahydrofolate (THF) supply
• Prevents Thymidylate Synthase from methylating dUMP to dTMP

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: How does the assembly sequence of a pyrimidine nucleotide differ fundamentally from that of a purine nucleotide?
back:
• Pyrimidine: The ring structure is synthesized entirely before being attached to PRPP
• Purine: The ring is built step-by-step directly onto the PRPP ribose-5-phosphate

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish between Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and II (CPS II) regarding their nitrogen source and metabolic pathway.
back:
• CPS I: Mitochondria, Urea Cycle, uses Ammonia (NH3)
• CPS II: Cytosol, Pyrimidine Synthesis, uses Glutamine

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the only mitochondrial enzyme involved in the de-novo pyrimidine biosynthetic pathway.
back:
• Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase
• Oxidizes dihydroorotate to orotic acid
• Associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting enzyme of de novo pyrimidine synthesis, which is located in the cytosol and inhibited by UTP, is [___].
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS-II)
• Stimulated by PRPP
• Inhibited by UTP (end-product inhibition)
• Uses Glutamine and CO2 as substrates

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia unresponsive to B12/folate and orotic acid crystals in the urine. Identify the likely enzyme deficiency.
back:
• UMP Synthase deficiency
• Condition: Hereditary Orotic Aciduria
• Results in failure to convert orotate to UMP
• Presents with growth retardation

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) in inhibiting DNA synthesis.
back:
• Acts as a 'suicide inhibitor'
• Targets Thymidylate Synthase
• Prevents conversion of dUMP to dTMP
• Depletes thymidine required for DNA replication

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the orotic aciduria seen in UMP Synthase deficiency with that seen in Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency.
back:
• UMP Synthase: Normal ammonia levels; Megaloblastic anemia present
• OTC Deficiency: Hyperammonemia present; Part of Urea Cycle defect
• OTC cause: Carbamoyl phosphate shunted to pyrimidine pathway

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the specific nitrogenous bases produced through the pyrimidine salvage pathway.
back:
• Cytosine, Uracil, and Thymine
• Utilizes nucleoside kinases (e.g., Uridine kinase)
• Uses ATP to phosphorylate nucleosides to nucleotides
• Less significant than purine salvage

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Unlike purine degradation which produces uric acid, pyrimidine ring catabolism results in highly soluble [___] and beta-aminoisobutyrate.
back:
• Beta-alanine
• Also produces NH3 and CO2
• Products are easily excreted in urine
• Does not lead to gout-like conditions

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient with orotic aciduria is treated with oral Uridine. Describe the biochemical rationale for this therapy.
back:
• Bypasses the enzymatic block (UMP Synthase)
• Salvaged to UMP by nucleoside kinases
• Provides feedback inhibition of CPS-II
• Reduces further orotic acid production

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the mechanism by which Methotrexate interferes with dTMP synthesis.
back:
• Inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR)
• Prevents regeneration of Tetrahydrofolate (THF)
• Depletes N5,N10-Methylene THF
• Indirectly halts Thymidylate Synthase activity

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish between de novo purine and pyrimidine synthesis regarding the timing of the ribose-5-phosphate (PRPP) addition.
back:
• Purines: Built directly onto the PRPP structure
• Pyrimidines: The ring is synthesized first, then attached to PRPP
• Intermediate of attachment: Orotic acid

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the three precursor molecules that contribute all atoms to the pyrimidine ring.
back:
• Aspartate (provides majority of ring atoms)
• Glutamine (amide nitrogen)
• CO2
• Aspartate contributes C4, C5, C6, and N1

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In mammalian de-novo pyrimidine synthesis, the regulated step is the formation of carbamoyl phosphate from glutamine and CO2, catalyzed by the cytosolic enzyme [___].
back:
* Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
* Inhibited by UTP.
* Activated by PRPP.
* Distinguished from CPS I of the urea cycle.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia and failure to thrive. Lab findings reveal high urinary orotic acid levels but normal blood ammonia. State the diagnosis and required treatment.
back:
* Diagnosis: Hereditary Orotic Aciduria.
* Defect: UMP Synthase deficiency.
* Treatment: Oral Uridine administration.
* Uridine bypasses the metabolic block to form UMP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of Ribonucleotide Reductase during the S-phase of the cell cycle regarding pyrimidine metabolism.
back:
* Converts pyrimidine ribonucleoside diphosphates (UDP, CDP) into deoxy-forms (dUDP, dCDP).
* Essential for DNA synthesis.
* Requires thioredoxin for reducing equivalents.
* Inhibited by dATP and hydroxyurea.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish between the orotic aciduria seen in UMP Synthase deficiency and that seen in Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency.
back:
* UMP Synthase: No hyperammonemia; presence of megaloblastic anemia.
* OTC Deficiency: Severe hyperammonemia present; part of urea cycle defect.
* Both involve orotic acid buildup but differ in nitrogen handling.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the metabolic fate of the pyrimidine ring during degradation and contrast the solubility of its products with purine end-products.
back:
* Ring is opened and degraded to Beta-alanine and Beta-aminoisobutyrate.
* Produces NH3 and CO2.
* Products are highly water-soluble.
* Contrasts with purines, which form insoluble uric acid.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The antineoplastic agent 5-Fluorouracil acts as a 'suicide inhibitor' by targeting the enzyme [___] to prevent dTMP synthesis.
back:
* Thymidylate Synthase.
* Competitively inhibits conversion of dUMP to dTMP.
* Requires N5,N10-methylene tetrahydrofolate.
* Directly halts DNA replication in rapidly dividing cells.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient on Methotrexate therapy develops dTMP deficiency. Relate the inhibition of Dihydrofolate Reductase to the pyrimidine synthesis pathway.
back:
* Inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase.
* Prevents regeneration of Tetrahydrofolate (THF) from DHF.
* Depletes N5,N10-methylene THF.
* This coenzyme is mandatory for Thymidylate Synthase activity.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the de-novo synthesis of pyrimidines with purines regarding when the ribose-5-phosphate (from PRPP) is added to the nitrogenous base.
back:
* Pyrimidines: The ring is synthesized first, then attached to PRPP.
* Purines: The ring is built atom-by-atom directly onto the PRPP structure.
* Parent nucleotide for pyrimidines is OMP; for purines is IMP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain how the cell utilizes the pyrimidine salvage pathway to mitigate the effects of UMP synthase deficiency.
back:
* Uses nucleoside kinases (e.g., Uridine kinase).
* Phosphorylates preformed pyrimidine nucleosides using ATP.
* Bypasses early de-novo steps (CPS II, CAD, Orotate).
* Provides UMP required for RNA/DNA synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the three molecules that contribute carbon and nitrogen atoms to the de-novo assembly of the pyrimidine ring.
back:
* Glutamine (Amide nitrogen).
* Aspartic Acid (most of the ring).
* CO2 (as bicarbonate).
* Aspartate contributes both Nitrogen and Carbon atoms.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The regulated step of de-novo pyrimidine synthesis in human cells is the formation of carbamoyl phosphate, catalyzed by the cytosolic enzyme [___].
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
• Activated by PRPP.
• Inhibited by UTP (end-product inhibition).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old presents with megaloblastic anemia and high urinary orotic acid, but normal blood ammonia. Name the deficient enzyme complex.
back:
• UMP Synthase (specifically Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase or OMP decarboxylase).
• Diagnosis: Hereditary Orotic Aciduria.
• Management: Oral Uridine administration.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the assembly order of the pyrimidine ring in relation to the ribose-5-phosphate sugar.
back:
• The pyrimidine ring is synthesized completely first as Orotic acid.
• It is subsequently attached to PRPP (ribose donor).
• This differs from purine synthesis, where the ring is built on the sugar.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the clinical outcome of pyrimidine degradation with that of purine degradation in humans.
back:
• Purines: Produce insoluble Uric acid (potential for Gout).
• Pyrimidines: Produce highly soluble β-alanine and β-aminoisobutyrate.
• Pyrimidine products are easily excreted without crystals/stones.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the three specific precursor molecules that contribute all atoms to the pyrimidine ring.
back:
• Glutamine (provides amide nitrogen).
• CO2 (Carbon Dioxide).
• Aspartic Acid (Aspartate).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Most pyrimidine synthesis occurs in the cytosol, but the enzyme [___] is uniquely located on the inner mitochondrial membrane.
back:
• Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase.
• Converts Dihydroorotate to Orotate.
• It is the only mitochondrial enzyme in this pathway.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient with colon cancer is treated with 5-Fluorouracil. Explain the molecular mechanism of its antitumor action.
back:
• Converted to 5-FdUMP.
• Suicide inhibition of Thymidylate Synthase.
• Depletes dTMP pools, halting DNA synthesis and cell division.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish between the nitrogen sources and pathways for CPS-I versus CPS-II.
back:
• CPS-I: Mitochondria; Urea Cycle; utilizes free Ammonia (NH3).
• CPS-II: Cytosol; Pyrimidine synthesis; utilizes Amide group of Glutamine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: How do Methotrexate and Trimethoprim indirectly inhibit the synthesis of dTMP from dUMP?
back:
• Both inhibit Dihydrofolate Reductase.
• Prevents regeneration of Tetrahydrofolate (THF).
• Deprives Thymidylate Synthase of its essential methylene-THF coenzyme.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the multi-functional polypeptide chain containing the first three enzymatic activities of pyrimidine synthesis.
back:
• CAD Protein.
• Includes: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II, Aspartate transcarbamoylase, and Dihydroorotase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In mammalian de novo pyrimidine synthesis, the cytosolic enzyme [___] serves as the primary regulated step and is allosterically inhibited by UTP.
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
• Activated by PRPP.
• Inhibited by UTP (end-product inhibition).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia and low height/weight; lab tests show excessive orotic acid in urine. Identify the deficient enzyme and the specific therapy.
back:
• Diagnosis: Hereditary Orotic Aciduria.
• Enzyme: UMP Synthase deficiency.
• Treatment: Uridine (salvaged to UMP, bypassing the metabolic block).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the coenzyme transformation that occurs when Thymidylate synthase methylates dUMP to form dTMP.
back:
• N5,N10-Methylene THF acts as the methyl donor.
• THF is oxidized to Dihydrofolate (DHF).
• Only reaction where THF serves as both a carbon donor and reducing agent.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: CPS I vs CPS II Isoenzymes
front: Contrast the metabolic pathway and nitrogen source between Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase (CPS) I and CPS II.
back:
• CPS I: Mitochondria; Urea Cycle; utilizes Ammonia (NH3).
• CPS II: Cytosol; Pyrimidine Synthesis; utilizes Glutamine (γ-amide group).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the three catalytic domains contained within the cytosolic multifunctional protein known as "CAD".
back:
• Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II.
• Aspartate transcarbamoylase.
• Dihydroorotase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: During the formation of orotic acid, the oxidation of dihydroorotate is catalyzed by [___], which is uniquely localized to the inner mitochondrial membrane.
back:
• Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase.
• All other pyrimidine synthesis enzymes are cytosolic.
• Produces Orotate (Orotic acid).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A cancer patient is treated with 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU). Explain the biochemical mechanism of its therapeutic "suicide inhibition."
back:
• 5-FU is converted to 5-FdUMP.
• Permanently binds/inactivates Thymidylate synthase.
• Prevents dTMP synthesis, halting DNA replication.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the biochemical fate and solubility of pyrimidine catabolic end-products compared to purines.
back:
• Pyrimidine: Ring is opened; produces β-alanine and β-aminoisobutyrate.
• Solubility: Highly soluble (unlike purine-derived uric acid).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Differentiate the timing of ribose 5-phosphate (from PRPP) addition in pyrimidine synthesis versus purine synthesis.
back:
• Pyrimidines: Ring is synthesized first, then attached to PRPP.
• Purines: Ring is built atom-by-atom directly onto a pre-existing PRPP molecule.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the three specific precursors that provide atoms for the assembly of the pyrimidine ring.
back:
• Glutamine (Amide nitrogen).
• CO2.
• Aspartic acid.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In mammalian cells, the rate-limiting and regulated step of de novo pyrimidine synthesis is catalyzed by [___], which is allosterically inhibited by UTP.
back:
• Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (CPS II)
• Located in the cytosol
• Activated by PRPP

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia and failure to thrive. Lab tests show massive excretion of orotic acid in urine, yet blood ammonia levels are normal. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
• Hereditary Orotic Aciduria
• Deficiency of UMP synthase (bifunctional enzyme)
• Treated with exogenous Uridine

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of N5, N10-methylene tetrahydrofolate during the conversion of dUMP to dTMP by thymidylate synthase.
back:
• Acts as a one-carbon methyl donor
• Acts as a reducing agent (donates 2 hydrogens)
• Oxidized to DHF (dihydrofolate) in the process

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and CPS II regarding their nitrogen source and metabolic pathway.
back:
• CPS I: Uses Ammonia (NH3); Urea Cycle
• CPS II: Uses Glutamine (γ-amide group); Pyrimidine Synthesis
• CPS I is mitochondrial; CPS II is cytosolic

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the three enzymatic domains contained within the multifunctional CAD polypeptide used in the initial stages of pyrimidine synthesis.
back:
• Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (C)
• Aspartate transcarbamoylase (A)
• Dihydroorotase (D)

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Unlike purine synthesis where the ring is built on a sugar, the pyrimidine ring is synthesized first and then attached to [___].
back:
• PRPP (5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate)
• Ribose 5-phosphate donor
• Catalyst: Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A cancer patient is prescribed 5-Fluorouracil. Explain the molecular mechanism by which this drug inhibits DNA synthesis.
back:
• Converted to 5-FdUMP
• Suicide inhibition of Thymidylate Synthase
• Depletes dTMP, halting DNA replication

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the physiological mechanism of dUTPase and its importance in maintaining DNA integrity.
back:
• Hydrolyzes dUTP to dUMP
• Limits dUTP availability for DNA polymerase
• Prevents erroneous incorporation of Uracil into DNA

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the end products of purine catabolism with the end products of pyrimidine catabolism in humans.
back:
• Purines: Uric acid (poorly soluble)
• Pyrimidines: β-alanine, β-aminoisobutyrate, NH3, and CO2 (highly soluble)

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the specific enzyme in the pyrimidine de novo pathway that is localized to the inner mitochondrial membrane rather than the cytosol.
back:
• Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
• Converts dihydroorotate to orotic acid
• All other de novo enzymes are cytosolic

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting enzyme in de novo pyrimidine synthesis, which is allosterically inhibited by UTP and activated by PRPP, is [___].
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
• Located in the cytosol.
• Uses glutamine and CO2 to form carbamoyl phosphate.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia (refractory to B12/Folate therapy), growth retardation, and high levels of orotic acid in the urine. Identify the deficiency and the standard treatment.
back:
• UMP Synthase deficiency (Hereditary Orotic Aciduria).
• Treatment: Oral Uridine.
• Uridine is salvaged to UMP, bypassing the block and providing feedback inhibition of the pathway.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) acts as a 'suicide inhibitor' in nucleotide metabolism.
back:
• 5-FU is converted to 5-FdUMP.
• Targets Thymidylate Synthase.
• Permanently binds the enzyme, blocking dUMP conversion to dTMP and halting DNA synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: CPS I vs CPS II Differentiation
front: Contrast Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and II (CPS II) regarding their cellular location and nitrogen source.
back:
• CPS I: Mitochondrial; uses Ammonia (NH3); part of Urea Cycle.
• CPS II: Cytosolic; uses Glutamine (amide group); part of Pyrimidine synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the primary highly-soluble end-products resulting from the degradation of the pyrimidine ring in humans.
back:
• Beta-alanine (from Uracil and Cytosine).
• Beta-aminoisobutyrate (from Thymine).
• CO2 and Ammonia (NH3).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: While most enzymes of pyrimidine de novo synthesis are cytosolic, the enzyme [___] is uniquely located on the inner mitochondrial membrane.
back:
• Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase.
• Catalyzes the oxidation of Dihydroorotate to Orotic acid (Orotate).
• Uses FAD as a coenzyme.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A cancer patient treated with Methotrexate shows a sharp decline in dTMP levels. Describe the mechanism of this specific metabolic depletion.
back:
• Methotrexate inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase.
• Prevents regeneration of Tetrahydrofolate (THF).
• Deprives Thymidylate Synthase of its methyl donor (N5,N10-methylene THF).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the fundamental difference in the sequence of ring assembly and ribose-5-phosphate attachment between purines and pyrimidines.
back:
• Purines: Ring is built atom-by-atom directly onto PRPP.
• Pyrimidines: The complete ring (Orotate) is synthesized first, then attached to PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the metabolic fate of the nitrogenous ring during purine versus pyrimidine degradation.
back:
• Purines: Ring remains intact; excreted as insoluble Uric Acid.
• Pyrimidines: Ring is opened/cleaved; excreted as highly soluble amino acids (Beta-alanine/Beta-aminoisobutyrate).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: List the three precursor molecules that contribute all atoms to the pyrimidine ring structure.
back:
• Aspartic Acid (Aspartate).
• Glutamine (Amide nitrogen).
• CO2.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In the de-novo pyrimidine synthesis pathway, the rate-limiting enzyme located in the cytosol is [___].
back:
Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
- Activated by PRPP.
- Inhibited by UTP.
- Uses Glutamine and CO2 as substrates.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia non-responsive to B12/Folate and high urinary orotic acid. Identify the most likely enzyme deficiency.
back:
UMP Synthase deficiency (Hereditary Orotic Aciduria).
- Affects orotate phosphoribosyltransferase or OMP decarboxylase.
- Leads to pyrimidine starvation.
- Treated with oral Uridine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of $N^5,N^{10}$-methylene tetrahydrofolate in the synthesis of dTMP.
back:
Acts as a one-carbon methyl donor.
- Required by Thymidylate Synthase.
- Converts dUMP to dTMP.
- It is oxidized to Dihydrofolate (DHF) during the reaction.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS-I) and Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS-II) based on cellular location and pathway.
back:
CPS-I: Mitochondria; Urea Cycle; activated by N-acetylglutamate.
- CPS-II: Cytosol; Pyrimidine de-novo synthesis; inhibited by UTP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the highly soluble nitrogenous end-products of pyrimidine catabolism.
back:
$̢$-alanine (from Cytosine/Uracil).
- $̢$-aminoisobutyrate (from Thymine).
- Both are excreted as CO2 and NH3.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The 'suicide inhibitor' that irreversibly binds to thymidylate synthase to stop DNA replication in cancer cells is [___].
back:
5-Fluorouracil (converted to 5-FdUMP).
- Thwarts dTMP production.
- Causes 'thymineless death' of cells.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient with orotic aciduria is prescribed Uridine. Describe the biochemical basis for this therapy.
back:
Salvage Pathway Activation.
- Uridine is phosphorylated to UMP by Uridine Kinase.
- Bypasses the defective UMP Synthase step.
- Provides pyrimidines for RNA/DNA synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: How does Methotrexate indirectly inhibit the production of dTMP?
back:
Inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR).
- Prevents regeneration of Tetrahydrofolate (THF).
- Depletes $N^5,N^{10}$-methylene THF required for Thymidylate Synthase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the de-novo synthesis of Purines versus Pyrimidines regarding the timing of ribose-5-phosphate addition.
back:
Purines: Ring is built atom-by-atom directly onto PRPP.
- Pyrimidines: The six-membered ring is synthesized first, then attached to PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the three catalytic activities contained within the multifunctional CAD protein in humans.
back:
Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II.
- Aspartate Transcarbamoylase.
- Dihydroorotase.
- These catalyze the first three steps of pyrimidine synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting and regulated step of de novo pyrimidine synthesis in human cells is catalyzed by the cytosolic enzyme [___].
back:
* Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
* Inhibited by UTP (feedback inhibition).
* Activated by PRPP.
* Uses glutamine and CO2 as substrates.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A child presents with megaloblastic anemia and low growth velocity. Labs show high urinary orotic acid but normal blood ammonia levels. Name the most likely deficient enzyme.
back:
* UMP Synthase deficiency.
* It is a bifunctional enzyme (Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase).
* Characterized by orotic aciduria without hyperammonemia.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of PRPP as both a substrate and a regulator in pyrimidine metabolism.
back:
* Substrate: Donates ribose 5-phosphate to orotate to form OMP.
* Activator: Allosterically stimulates CPS II to increase de novo synthesis rate.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the orotic aciduria seen in UMP Synthase deficiency with that seen in Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency.
back:
* UMP Synthase Deficiency: Megaloblastic anemia; normal ammonia.
* OTC Deficiency: Hyperammonemia and CNS symptoms; no anemia.
* OTC deficiency shunts carbamoyl phosphate into pyrimidine synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the specific enzymatic step targeted by the 'suicide inhibitor' 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU).
back:
* Inhibits Thymidylate Synthase.
* Prevents conversion of dUMP to dTMP.
* Depletes dTMP pools, halting DNA synthesis and cell division.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Unlike the insoluble uric acid produced from purines, the pyrimidine thymine is degraded into the highly soluble end-product [___].
back:
* ̢̢̢-aminoisobutyrate.
* Further degraded to CO2 and NH3.
* High solubility prevents crystal formation/gout-like symptoms.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
