front: A patient with UMP Synthase deficiency is treated with Uridine. Describe the biochemical rationale for why this alleviates both the anemia and the orotic aciduria.
back:
* Salvage: Uridine is converted to UMP by nucleoside kinases.
* Feedback: Resulting UTP inhibits CPS II, stopping orotic acid overproduction.
* Bypass: Provides pyrimidines needed for RNA/DNA synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: How does the assembly of the pyrimidine ring differ fundamentally from the assembly of the purine ring regarding Ribose 5-Phosphate?
back:
* Pyrimidines: The ring is synthesized completely before attachment to ribose (PRPP).
* Purines: The ring is built atom-by-atom directly onto the ribose (PRPP) foundation.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the interaction between Methotrexate and the conversion of dUMP to dTMP.
back:
* Methotrexate inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase.
* Depletes Tetrahydrofolate (THF).
* THF is required to regenerate N5,N10-methylene THF for dTMP synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the only enzyme of the de novo pyrimidine pathway located in the mitochondria.
back:
* Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase.
* Converts dihydroorotate to orotic acid.
* All other enzymes (CAD and UMP synthase complexes) are cytosolic.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting enzyme of de novo pyrimidine synthesis, which is located in the cytosol and stimulated by PRPP while being inhibited by UTP, is [___].
back: • Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (CPS II) • Utilizes Glutamine and CO2 as substrates • Primary regulated step in the pathway.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 9-month-old infant presents with failure to thrive and megaloblastic anemia that is unresponsive to Vitamin B12 or folate. Urine analysis reveals high levels of orotic acid. This condition is caused by a deficiency in [___].
back: • UMP Synthase (bifunctional enzyme) • Contains Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and Orotidylate decarboxylase domains • Causes Hereditary Orotic Aciduria.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain why the construction of the pyrimidine ring is considered fundamentally different from the construction of the purine ring regarding the use of PRPP.
back: • Pyrimidines: The ring is fully synthesized (as orotate) before being attached to PRPP. • Purines: The ring is built directly onto the PRPP scaffold from the start.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the clinical management and biochemical findings of a patient with UMP Synthase deficiency versus one with Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency.
back: • UMP Synthase: Treated with Uridine; presents with megaloblastic anemia and normal ammonia. • OTC Deficiency: Treated with protein restriction; presents with hyperammonemia and no anemia.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Detail the specific enzymatic step targeted by the chemotherapeutic agent 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU).
back: • Inhibits Thymidylate Synthase • Prevents the conversion of dUMP to dTMP • Acts as a 'suicide inhibitor' after conversion to 5-FdUMP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Diagnostic confirmation of Hereditary Orotic Aciduria typically requires the finding of high urinary orotic acid and the presence of [___] on a peripheral blood smear.
back: • Megaloblastic anemia (macrocytic RBCs) • Hypersegmented neutrophils • Distinguishes it from urea cycle defects which lack hematological findings.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis is prescribed Leflunomide. Describe how this drug inhibits the proliferation of activated T-cells via the pyrimidine pathway.
back: • Inhibits Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase • Blocks the conversion of dihydroorotate to orotate • Specifically targets the inner mitochondrial membrane step.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which exogenous Uridine administration successfully treats the symptoms of Hereditary Orotic Aciduria.
back: • Uridine is salvaged to UMP and then UTP. • UTP acts as a feedback inhibitor of CPS II. • This reduces orotic acid overproduction and provides necessary pyrimidines.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Differentiate between Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and CPS II regarding their cellular location and metabolic role.
back: • CPS I: Mitochondria; involved in the Urea Cycle (uses ammonia). • CPS II: Cytosol; involved in Pyrimidine Synthesis (uses glutamine).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the highly soluble end products resulting from the degradation of cytosine and uracil in humans.
back: • Beta-alanine • Ammonia (NH3) • Carbon dioxide (CO2) • (Note: Thymine degrades to beta-aminoisobutyrate).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting enzyme of de novo pyrimidine synthesis, which resides in the cytosol and is inhibited by UTP, is [___].
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
• Activated by PRPP.
• Inhibited by UTP (end-product inhibition).
• Part of the multifunctional CAD protein complex.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A child presents with megaloblastic anemia, growth retardation, and orotic aciduria. Explain the biochemical rationale for administering oral uridine to this patient.
back:
• Bypasses the deficient UMP Synthase enzyme.
• Uridine is salvaged to UMP via nucleoside kinases.
• Restores pyrimidine pools for DNA/RNA synthesis.
• Decreases orotate excretion via feedback inhibition.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the biological role of Ribonucleotide Reductase and its essential cofactors during the S-phase of the cell cycle.
back:
• Converts ribonucleoside diphosphates (NDPs) to deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates (dNDPs).
• Requires Thioredoxin as a hydrogen donor.
• Regulated by dATP (inhibitor) and ATP (activator).
• Crucial for providing substrates for DNA replication.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: CPS I vs CPS II Comparison
front: Contrast the metabolic localization and nitrogen sources of Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
back:
• Localization: CPS I is mitochondrial (Urea Cycle); CPS II is cytosolic (Pyrimidines).
• Nitrogen Source: CPS I uses free Ammonia; CPS II uses Glutamine.
• Regulators: CPS I requires N-acetylglutamate; CPS II is activated by PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the target enzyme of 5-Fluorouracil and its specific effect on pyrimidine metabolism.
back:
• Inhibits Thymidylate Synthase.
• Acts as a suicide inhibitor (as 5-FdUMP).
• Blocks dUMP conversion to dTMP.
• Results in 'thymineless death' of rapidly dividing cells.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: During the final catabolism of the pyrimidine thymine, the unique, highly soluble end-product excreted in urine is [___].
back:
• β-aminoisobutyrate.
• Also produces CO2 and NH3.
• Pyrimidine rings (unlike purines) are completely cleaved.
• Metabolites are highly soluble, preventing 'gout-like' conditions.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient undergoing chemotherapy with Methotrexate develops dTMP deficiency. Which specific folate-related step is interrupted by this drug?
back:
• Inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR).
• Prevents regeneration of Tetrahydrofolate (THF) from DHF.
• Depletes N5,N10-methylene THF required for thymidylate synthesis.
• Indirectly halts DNA synthesis by limiting dTMP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the biochemical requirements and enzyme responsible for the conversion of UTP to Cytidine Triphosphate (CTP).
back:
• Catalyzed by CTP Synthetase.
• Nitrogen Donor: Glutamine.
• Energy Source: ATP hydrolysis.
• Occurs at the triphosphate level after UMP phosphorylation.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the sequence of ring assembly and PRPP attachment in de novo purine vs. pyrimidine synthesis.
back:
• Purines: Ring is built atom-by-atom directly onto PRPP.
• Pyrimidines: Six-membered ring is synthesized first, then attached to PRPP.
• Initial common intermediate: PRPP is used in both pathways.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: List the three essential precursors that contribute atoms to the pyrimidine ring structure.
back:
• Glutamine (provides Amide Nitrogen).
• Aspartic Acid (provides multiple C and N atoms).
• CO2 (provides Carbon).
• PRPP provides the ribose-5-phosphate sugar later.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The regulated step of pyrimidine de-novo synthesis in mammalian cells is the production of [___] from glutamine and CO2.
back:
• Carbamoyl phosphate
• Catalyzed by Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS-II)
• Activated by PRPP and inhibited by UTP

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia, poor growth, and high levels of orotic acid in the urine. Blood ammonia levels are normal. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back:
• Orotic Aciduria
• Due to deficiency of UMP Synthase (bifunctional enzyme)
• Treated with exogenous Uridine to bypass the metabolic block

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: How does the role of Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS-II) differ from CPS-I in cellular metabolism?
back:
• CPS-II: Cytosolic; used for pyrimidine synthesis; uses glutamine as nitrogen donor
• CPS-I: Mitochondrial; used for urea cycle; uses ammonia as nitrogen donor

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the biochemical findings used to distinguish between Orotic Aciduria caused by UMP Synthase deficiency versus Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency.
back:
• UMP Synthase Deficiency: Megaloblastic anemia; normal ammonia levels
• OTC Deficiency: Hyperammonemia; no megaloblastic anemia (due to urea cycle failure)

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the specific metabolic step targeted by 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) and its effect on DNA synthesis.
back:
• Inhibits Thymidylate Synthase
• Acts as a suicide inhibitor (as 5-FdUMP)
• Prevents conversion of dUMP to dTMP, halting DNA replication

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Unlike the purine ring, the pyrimidine ring is constructed [___] being attached to the ribose 5-phosphate donated by PRPP.
back:
• Before
• The completed pyrimidine ring (Orotic acid) is synthesized first
• Orotate Phosphoribosyltransferase then adds the PRPP moiety

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient undergoing chemotherapy is given Methotrexate. Explain why this drug inhibits the synthesis of Thymidine Monophosphate (TMP).
back:
• Inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR)
• Prevents regeneration of Tetrahydrofolate (THF)
• THF is required by Thymidylate Synthase as a one-carbon donor

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the biological significance of UTP Diphosphatase (dUTPase) in preventing DNA mutations.
back:
• Hydrolyzes dUTP to dUMP
• Reduces availability of dUTP as a substrate for DNA polymerase
• Prevents the erroneous incorporation of Uracil into DNA

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the end-products of pyrimidine degradation with those of purine degradation in humans.
back:
• Pyrimidines: Highly soluble products (beta-alanine, beta-aminoisobutyrate, CO2, NH3)
• Purines: Relatively insoluble Uric acid
• Pyrimidine rings are opened, whereas purine rings remain intact

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the three molecules that contribute atoms to the formation of the pyrimidine ring.
back:
• Aspartic acid
• Glutamine (amide nitrogen)
• Carbon Dioxide (CO2)

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting enzyme in de novo pyrimidine synthesis, which is located in the cytosol and inhibited by UTP, is [___].
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
• Activated by PRPP.
• Uses Glutamine and CO2 as substrates.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia non-responsive to Vitamin B12 and high urinary orotic acid. This condition is caused by a deficiency in [___].
back:
• UMP Synthase (bifunctional enzyme).
• Domains: Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase.
• Leads to hereditary Orotic Aciduria.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the mechanism by which 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) inhibits DNA synthesis.
back:
• Converted to 5-FdUMP.
• Acts as a 'suicide inhibitor' of Thymidylate Synthase.
• Blocks dUMP to dTMP conversion, depleting thymidine for DNA.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the diagnostic lab findings of UMP Synthase deficiency versus Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency regarding ammonia.
back:
• UMP Synthase: Normal blood ammonia levels.
• OTC Deficiency: Hyperammonemia (due to Urea Cycle defect) alongside orotic aciduria.
• Both present with urinary orotic acid.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the specific mitochondrial enzyme involved in the otherwise cytosolic de novo pyrimidine pathway.
back:
• Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase.
• Located on the inner mitochondrial membrane.
• Converts dihydroorotate to orotate.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In the de novo synthesis of pyrimidines, the [___] ring is completely synthesized before it is attached to the ribose-5-phosphate sugar.
back:
• Pyrimidine (Orotate) ring.
• Contrast: In purine synthesis, the ring is built directly onto PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient with hereditary orotic aciduria shows symptomatic improvement and decreased orotate excretion after treatment with [___].
back:
• Uridine.
• Salvaged by nucleoside kinases to UMP.
• Bypasses the metabolic block at UMP Synthase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: How does Methotrexate treatment result in the depletion of thymidine monophosphate (dTMP)?
back:
• Inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR).
• Prevents regeneration of Tetrahydrofolate (THF).
• Depletes N5,N10-methylene THF required by Thymidylate Synthase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the clinical significance of the end products of purine degradation versus pyrimidine degradation.
back:
• Purines: Uric acid (poorly soluble; causes Gout).
• Pyrimidines: Beta-alanine and Beta-aminoisobutyrate (highly soluble; no known pathology).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: List the three primary precursor molecules that donate atoms to the pyrimidine ring structure.
back:
• Glutamine (amide nitrogen).
• Aspartic acid.
• CO2 (Bicarbonate).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The three primary precursors that contribute atoms to the pyrimidine ring are aspartate, CO2, and [___].
back:
• Glutamine (provides the amide nitrogen)
• Aspartic acid
• Carbon dioxide

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old presents with megaloblastic anemia, poor growth, and high urinary orotic acid. Blood ammonia is normal. Identify the deficient enzyme.
back:
• UMP Synthase (Hereditary Orotic Aciduria)
• Bifunctional enzyme: Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase
• Treatment: Oral Uridine

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: How is Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II) regulated as the committed step of pyrimidine synthesis?
back:
• Activated by: PRPP (feed-forward)
• Inhibited by: UTP (feedback inhibition)
• Occurs in the cytosol

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: CPS I vs CPS II Distinction
front: Contrast Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and CPS II regarding cellular location and metabolic pathway.
back:
• CPS I: Mitochondria; Urea cycle
• CPS II: Cytosol; De-novo pyrimidine synthesis
• CPS I nitrogen source: Ammonia
• CPS II nitrogen source: Glutamine

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Mechanistically, how does 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) halt the synthesis of dTMP during chemotherapy?
back:
• Suicide inhibition of Thymidylate Synthase
• Converted to 5-FdUMP
• Permanently binds the enzyme, preventing dUMP to dTMP conversion

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In the catabolism of pyrimidine nucleotides, the specific end-product of thymine degradation is [___].
back:
• β-aminoisobutyrate
• Highly soluble product
• Uracil/Cytosine degrade to β-alanine

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient on Methotrexate therapy shows decreased dTMP levels. Explain the underlying biochemical reason.
back:
• Inhibition of Dihydrofolate Reductase
• Depletes Tetrahydrofolate (THF)
• Prevents N5,N10-methylene THF regeneration required for Thymidylate Synthase

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the structural sequence difference between de-novo purine and pyrimidine ring construction.
back:
• Purines: Built atom-by-atom directly onto a pre-existing PRPP molecule
• Pyrimidines: Ring (Orotic acid) is synthesized first, then attached to PRPP

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish the salvage of pyrimidines from the salvage of purines in human cells.
back:
• Purines: Use phosphoribosyltransferases (HGPRT/APRT) to salvage free bases
• Pyrimidines: Primarily salvage nucleosides via kinases (e.g., Uridine kinase)
• Pyrimidine base salvage is minimal

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the only enzyme of the de-novo pyrimidine pathway that is not located in the cytosol.
back:
• Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase
• Located on the inner mitochondrial membrane
• Converts Dihydroorotate to Orotic acid

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting enzyme of de-novo pyrimidine synthesis in humans, which is inhibited by UTP and activated by PRPP, is [___].
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
• Located in the cytosol.
• Utilizes glutamine and CO2 as substrates.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A child presents with megaloblastic anemia non-responsive to B12/Folate and high levels of orotic acid in the urine. This condition results from a deficiency in the bifunctional enzyme [___].
back:
• UMP Synthase.
• Composed of Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase.
• Treatment involves oral uridine supplementation.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: CPS I vs CPS II Distinction
front: Explain the difference between Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and II (CPS II) regarding location and pathway.
back:
• CPS I: Mitochondrial; involved in the Urea Cycle.
• CPS II: Cytosolic; involved in Pyrimidine Synthesis.
• CPS I uses ammonia; CPS II uses glutamine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the clinical findings of Orotic Aciduria caused by UMP Synthase deficiency versus Ornithine Transcarbamoylase (OTC) deficiency.
back:
• UMP Synthase Deficiency: Megaloblastic anemia with normal blood ammonia.
• OTC Deficiency: Severe hyperammonemia (lethargy/coma) without megaloblastic anemia.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain how 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) pharmacologically inhibits the synthesis of thymidine monophosphate (dTMP).
back:
• Converted to 5-FdUMP.
• Acts as a suicide inhibitor of Thymidylate Synthase.
• Depletes dTMP, halting DNA replication.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: To bypass the metabolic block in hereditary orotic aciduria and provide a source for pyrimidine salvage, the nucleoside [___] is administered.
back:
• Uridine.
• Converted to UMP via salvage pathway.
• Feedback inhibits CPS II, reducing orotate production.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient on Methotrexate therapy shows reduced dTMP levels. Describe the conceptual application of this drug on the folate cycle.
back:
• Inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR).
• Prevents regeneration of Tetrahydrofolate (THF).
• Starves Thymidylate Synthase of N5,N10-methylene THF.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the only enzyme in the de-novo pyrimidine pathway located in the inner mitochondrial membrane and its specific reaction.
back:
• Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase.
• Oxidizes Dihydroorotate to Orotic acid (Orotate).
• Linked to the electron transport chain.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the initial assembly of the nitrogenous ring in purine synthesis versus pyrimidine synthesis.
back:
• Purine: Built directly onto a pre-existing ribose 5-phosphate (PRPP).
• Pyrimidine: The ring (Orotate) is synthesized first, then attached to PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: List the highly soluble end-products of pyrimidine ring degradation in humans.
back:
• beta-alanine (from Cytosine/Uracil).
• beta-aminoisobutyrate (from Thymine).
• Carbon dioxide and Ammonia.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The cytosolic enzyme that serves as the regulated, rate-limiting step in de-novo pyrimidine synthesis is [___].
back:
• Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (CPS II).
• Inhibited by UTP (end-product inhibition).
• Activated by PRPP (feed-forward activation).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A child presents with megaloblastic anemia, poor growth, and high levels of orotic acid in the urine. Administration of [___] bypasses the metabolic block in this condition.
back:
• Uridine.
• Diagnosis: Orotic Aciduria (UMP Synthase deficiency).
• Uridine is salvaged to UMP by nucleoside kinases, bypassing the de-novo block.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the mechanism by which 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) inhibits DNA synthesis in rapidly dividing cancer cells.
back:
• Metabolically converted to 5-FdUMP.
• Acts as a 'suicide inhibitor' of Thymidylate Synthase.
• Permanently binds the enzyme, stopping dUMP conversion to dTMP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the clinical presentation of UMP Synthase deficiency with Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency regarding ammonia levels and hematology.
back:
• UMP Synthase: Normal ammonia levels; Megaloblastic anemia present.
• OTC Deficiency: Severe hyperammonemia (urea cycle defect); No megaloblastic anemia.
• Both show orotic aciduria.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the specific donor molecule that provides both the methyl group and hydrogen atoms for the conversion of dUMP to dTMP.
back:
• N5,N10-Methylene Tetrahydrofolate.
• It is oxidized to Dihydrofolate (DHF) during the reaction.
• Catalyzed by Thymidylate Synthase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Unlike other enzymes of the de-novo pyrimidine pathway which are cytosolic, Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase is uniquely localized in the [___].
back:
• Inner mitochondrial membrane.
• It catalyzes the oxidation of dihydroorotate to orotic acid.
• Uses FMN as a coenzyme.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient on Methotrexate therapy shows a decrease in dTMP production. This is due to the inhibition of [___], which prevents the regeneration of tetrahydrofolate.
back:
• Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR).
• Prevents the reduction of DHF back to THF.
• Leads to a shortage of the one-carbon donors needed for dTMP synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the solubility and clinical significance of pyrimidine degradation products compared to purine degradation products.
back:
• Products: Beta-alanine, Beta-aminoisobutyrate, NH3, and CO2.
• Clinically: Products are highly water-soluble.
• Unlike purines (uric acid), pyrimidine degradation does not lead to crystal deposition or gout.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish between Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and CPS II based on their metabolic pathways and nitrogen sources.
back:
• CPS I: Mitochondria; Urea Cycle; Source is Ammonia (NH3).
• CPS II: Cytosol; Pyrimidine Synthesis; Source is Glutamine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: List the two catalytic domains found on the bifunctional cytosolic protein known as UMP Synthase.
back:
• Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase (OPRT).
• OMP decarboxylase.
• Deficiency of either/both causes hereditary orotic aciduria.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The cytosolic enzyme that serves as the rate-limiting and regulated step in de novo pyrimidine synthesis is [___].
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II)
• Inhibited by UTP (end-product inhibition)
• Activated by PRPP
• Uses Glutamine as the nitrogen source

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia unresponsive to B12/Folate therapy and orotic acid crystals in the urine. Identify the likely enzyme deficiency.
back:
• UMP Synthase deficiency
• Condition: Hereditary Orotic Aciduria
• Affects bifunctional domains: Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase
• Treatment: Oral Uridine

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of N5, N10-Methylene Tetrahydrofolate in the conversion of dUMP to dTMP.
back:
• Acts as a methyl group donor
• Catalyzed by Thymidylate Synthase
• THF is oxidized to Dihydrofolate (DHF)
• Only reaction where THF is consumed as a redox agent

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the orotic aciduria seen in Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency versus UMP Synthase deficiency.
back:
• OTC Deficiency: Associated with hyperammonemia; excess carbamoyl phosphate leaks into pyrimidine pathway.
• UMP Synthase Deficiency: No hyperammonemia; associated with megaloblastic anemia.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the highly soluble end-products resulting from the degradation of the pyrimidine ring.
back:
• Uracil/Cytosine: β-alanine
• Thymine: β-aminoisobutyrate
• General products: CO2 and Ammonia (NH3)

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The pyrimidine analog used in cancer therapy that acts as a 'suicide inhibitor' of thymidylate synthase is [___].
back:
• 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU)
• Converted to 5-FdUMP intracellularly
• Irreversibly binds the enzyme
• Inhibits DNA synthesis

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient with Hereditary Orotic Aciduria is treated with Uridine. Describe the pathway used to bypass the metabolic block.
back:
• Pyrimidine Salvage Pathway
• Uridine is phosphorylated by Uridine Kinase
• Converted directly to UMP
• Provides pyrimidines for RNA/DNA without de novo synthesis

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the unique cellular localization and redox requirement of Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase.
back:
• Located in Inner Mitochondrial Membrane
• All other pyrimidine enzymes are cytosolic
• Oxidizes Dihydroorotate to Orotate
• Uses Coenzyme Q (Ubiquinone) as electron acceptor

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and II (CPS II) regarding their biological role.
back:
• CPS I: Mitochondrial; Urea cycle; Nitrogen source is NH3; Activated by N-acetylglutamate.
• CPS II: Cytosolic; Pyrimidine synthesis; Nitrogen source is Glutamine; Inhibited by UTP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Role of PRPP in Nucleotide Synthesis
front: Name the activated pentose sugar that provides the ribose 5-phosphate donor for pyrimidine nucleotide formation.
back:
• PRPP (5-Phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate)
• Added to Orotate to form OMP
• Donor for both de novo and salvage pathways

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting and regulated step in mammalian de novo pyrimidine synthesis is catalyzed by the cytosolic enzyme [___].
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
• Activated by PRPP (feed-forward).
• Inhibited by UTP (feedback inhibition).
• Uses Glutamine as the nitrogen donor.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia and low height. Lab tests show massive urinary orotic acid. This condition is caused by a deficiency in [___].
back:
• UMP Synthase (bifunctional enzyme).
• Domains involved: Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase.
• Leads to blocked UMP production.
• Treated with oral Uridine to bypass the defect.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) in inhibiting dTMP production during pyrimidine metabolism.
back:
• Converted to 5-FdUMP (active form).
• Acts as a 'suicide inhibitor' of Thymidylate Synthase.
• Permanently binds the enzyme.
• Prevents methylation of dUMP to dTMP, halting DNA synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: CPS I vs CPS II Isoenzymes
front: Contrast the nitrogen sources and cellular locations of Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) vs. Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
back:
• CPS I: Mitochondrial; uses free ammonia (NH3) for the urea cycle.
• CPS II: Cytosolic; uses the amide group of Glutamine for pyrimidine synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the specific precursors that contribute atoms to the formation of the pyrimidine ring.
back:
• Glutamine (Amide nitrogen).
• Aspartic Acid (provides most of the ring).
• Carbon Dioxide (CO2).
• Requires PRPP to form the final nucleotide.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Unlike purine synthesis, the pyrimidine ring is first fully synthesized as [___] before being attached to the ribose-5-phosphate donor, PRPP.
back:
• Orotic Acid (Orotate).
• Reaction catalyzed by Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase.
• Produces Orotidine monophosphate (OMP).
• This avoids building the ring directly on the sugar.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient on Methotrexate therapy shows inhibited pyrimidine synthesis. Describe the metabolic block causing this effect.
back:
• Inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR).
• Depletes Tetrahydrofolate (THF) stores.
• Starves Thymidylate Synthase of its coenzyme (N5,N10-methylene THF).
• Directly prevents dUMP conversion to dTMP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the degradation pathway of the pyrimidine ring compared to the purine ring in humans.
back:
• Pyrimidine ring is opened and cleaved (purines are not).
• End products: β-alanine and β-aminoisobutyrate.
• Produces CO2 and NH3.
• Products are highly water-soluble.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the metabolic efficiency of the De-Novo pathway versus the Pyrimidine Salvage pathway.
back:
• De-Novo: High energy cost; uses amino acids and CO2.
• Salvage: Low energy; uses nucleoside kinases (e.g., Uridine kinase) to recycle preformed bases/nucleosides.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the enzyme that reduces ribonucleoside diphosphates to deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates and its key inhibitor.
back:
• Enzyme: Ribonucleotide Reductase (RNR).
• Requires Thioredoxin as a cofactor.
• Inhibited by high levels of dATP.
• Targeted by the drug Hydroxyurea.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In de novo pyrimidine synthesis, the regulated, rate-limiting step occurs in the cytosol and is catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II)
• Inhibited by: UTP (end-product)
• Activated by: PRPP

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia, poor growth, and high levels of orotic acid in the urine. Blood ammonia is normal. Identify the deficient enzyme.
back:
• UMP Synthase (bifunctional enzyme)
• Specific domains: Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and Orotidylate decarboxylase
• Treatment: Oral Uridine

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the biochemical role of N5, N10-Methylene Tetrahydrofolate during the synthesis of dTMP from dUMP.
back:
• Acts as a one-carbon donor (methyl group)
• Acts as a reducing agent (donating hydrogens)
• Oxidized to Dihydrofolate (DHF) during the reaction

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the metabolic cause of orotic aciduria in UMP Synthase deficiency with that in Urea Cycle defects like OTC deficiency.
back:
• UMP Synthase Deficiency: Inability to convert orotate to UMP
• OTC Deficiency: Excess mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate leaks to cytosol, fueling orotate overproduction
• Differentiation: OTC deficiency shows hyperammonemia; UMP synthase deficiency does not

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: List the final, highly soluble end products of pyrimidine ring degradation in humans.
back:
• Beta-alanine
• Beta-aminoisobutyrate
• CO2 and Ammonia (NH3)

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The antineoplastic drug 5-Fluorouracil functions as a 'suicide inhibitor' by metabolically converting to 5-FdUMP and binding to [___].
back:
• Thymidylate Synthase
• Result: Depletion of dTMP levels
• Clinical effect: Inhibition of DNA synthesis

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A laboratory study involves inhibiting the 'CAD' multifunctional protein. Which three enzymatic activities are being disrupted?
back:
• Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II
• Aspartate transcarbamoylase
• Dihydroorotase
• Significance: These catalyze the first three steps of pyrimidine synthesis

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the specific mechanism and nitrogen source required for the conversion of UTP to Cytidine Triphosphate (CTP).
back:
• Enzyme: CTP Synthetase
• Nitrogen Donor: Glutamine (amide group)
• Energy source: ATP required for the amination

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and II (CPS II) regarding their cellular location and nitrogen source.
back:
• CPS I: Mitochondria; uses Ammonia (NH3) for Urea cycle
• CPS II: Cytosol; uses Glutamine for Pyrimidine synthesis

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the three molecular precursors that provide all the atoms for the de novo construction of the pyrimidine ring.
back:
• Aspartic acid
• Glutamine (amide nitrogen)
• CO2 (Bicarbonate)

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting enzyme in de novo pyrimidine synthesis, which is inhibited by UTP and activated by PRPP, is [___].
back:
Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
- Located in the cytosol.
- Part of the CAD multifunctional polypeptide.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A child presents with growth retardation and megaloblastic anemia unresponsive to B12 or Folate. Labs show excessive orotic acid in urine. Identify the deficient bifunctional enzyme.
back:
UMP Synthase.
- Possesses orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase domains.
- Causes hereditary Orotic Aciduria.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the distinct roles of PRPP in the pyrimidine de novo pathway compared to the purine de novo pathway.
back: In purine synthesis, PRPP is the starting scaffold. In pyrimidine synthesis, the ring (orotate) is synthesized first and then attached to PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient with Hyperammonemia and Orotic Aciduria is suspected of a urea cycle defect. Contrast this with Orotic Aciduria caused by UMP synthase deficiency.
back:
- OTC Deficiency: High ammonia; carbamoyl phosphate spills into pyrimidines.
- UMP Synthase Deficiency: Normal ammonia; characterized by megaloblastic anemia and growth failure.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the specific metabolic fate of the pyrimidine ring during degradation in human cells.
back:
The pyrimidine ring is cleaved and opened.
- Degraded to highly soluble end-products: ̢-alanine and ̢-aminoisobutyrate.
- Produces ammonia (NH3) and CO2.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The methyl group donor required for the conversion of dUMP to dTMP by thymidylate synthase is [___].
back:
N5,N10-Methylene tetrahydrofolate.
- It is oxidized to Dihydrofolate (DHF) during the reaction.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is administered for colorectal cancer. Identify the specific nucleotide it mimics and the enzyme it irreversibly inhibits.
back:
- Mimics: dUMP.
- Enzyme: Thymidylate Synthase.
- Mechanism: Suicide inhibition prevents dTMP/DNA synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe how Uridine administration alleviates the clinical symptoms and biochemical markers of hereditary Orotic Aciduria.
back:
- Salvage: Uridine is converted to UMP by nucleoside kinases.
- Inhibition: UMP inhibits CPS II, reducing orotic acid production.
- Supply: Restores pyrimidine pools for DNA/RNA synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II) regarding their cellular location and nitrogen source.
back:
- CPS I: Mitochondria; uses Ammonia (NH3) as nitrogen source.
- CPS II: Cytosol; uses Glutamine as nitrogen source.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: List the three specific precursor molecules that provide atoms for the pyrimidine ring.
back:
- Glutamine (amide nitrogen).
- Aspartic Acid.
- CO2.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In the de novo synthesis of pyrimidines, the regulated and committed step occurs in the cytosol and is catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back:
Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
- Inhibited by: UTP (end product).
- Activated by: PRPP.
- Nitrogen Source: Glutamine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia, poor growth, and high levels of orotic acid in the urine. Blood ammonia levels are normal. Identify the deficient enzyme.
back:
UMP Synthase.
- It is a bifunctional enzyme (Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase).
- Treatment: Oral uridine supplementation bypasses the metabolic block.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the timing of ribose 5-phosphate (PRPP) addition in pyrimidine synthesis compared to the purine synthesis pathway.
back:
- Pyrimidines: The heterocyclic ring is synthesized completely before being attached to PRPP.
- Purines: The ring is built directly onto a pre-existing PRPP molecule atom-by-atom.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A male infant presents with hyperammonemia and orotic aciduria. Contrast the likely enzyme deficiency in this patient with that of a patient having orotic aciduria and normal ammonia.
back:
- Hyperammonemia: Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency (Urea cycle defect).
- Normal Ammonia: UMP Synthase deficiency (De novo pyrimidine synthesis defect).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the 'suicide inhibitor' that is metabolically converted to 5-FdUMP to permanently inactivate thymidylate synthase.
back:
5-Fluorouracil (5-FU).
- Mechanism: Prevents conversion of dUMP to dTMP.
- Clinical Use: Chemotherapeutic agent for various cancers (e.g., colorectal).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Unlike the purine ring which remains intact in humans, the pyrimidine ring is cleaved into highly soluble end-products, specifically [___] and beta-aminoisobutyrate.
back:
Beta-alanine.
- Other products: NH3 and CO2.
- Solubility: These products are highly soluble and do not cause conditions like gout.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A cancer patient is treated with Methotrexate. Describe the specific impact of this drug on the production of dTMP from dUMP.
back:
- Inhibits: Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR).
- Effect: Depletes Tetrahydrofolate (THF) supply.
- Consequence: Prevents the methylation of dUMP, stopping DNA synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the biological function of dUTPase (UTP diphosphatase) in preventing DNA mutations.
back:
- Function: Rapidly hydrolyzes dUTP to dUMP.
- Purpose: Lowers dUTP availability to prevent the erroneous incorporation of uracil into DNA instead of thymine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the nitrogen source and cellular location of Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and II.
back:
- CPS I: Uses Ammonia (NH3); Mitochondria (Urea cycle).
- CPS II: Uses Glutamine; Cytosol (Pyrimidine synthesis).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: List the three precursor molecules that contribute all atoms to the pyrimidine ring.
back:
1. Aspartate.
2. Glutamine (amide nitrogen).
3. CO2 (as bicarbonate).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting and regulated step of de novo pyrimidine synthesis in human cytosolic cells is catalyzed by [___].
back:
Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
- Inhibited by UTP (end product).
- Activated by PRPP (substrate availability).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia non-responsive to Vitamin B12, physical growth retardation, and crystalline sediment in the urine. Identify the deficient bifunctional enzyme.
back:
UMP Synthase.
- Deficient in Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and Orotidylate decarboxylase.
- Causes massive excretion of orotic acid in urine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the role of Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR) in the production of thymidine nucleotides.
back:
- DHFR reduces Dihydrofolate back to Tetrahydrofolate (THF).
- THF is required by Thymidylate Synthase to methylate dUMP into dTMP.
- Inhibition (e.g., by Methotrexate) stops DNA synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: CPS I vs CPS II Differential
front: Contrast the location and nitrogen source of Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) with Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
back:
- CPS I: Mitochondria; uses free Ammonia (NH3); involved in Urea Cycle.
- CPS II: Cytosol; uses Glutamine (gamma-amide group); involved in Pyrimidine synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the biochemical mechanism of 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) as an antineoplastic agent.
back:
- Converted to 5-FdUMP.
- Acts as a 'suicide inhibitor' of Thymidylate Synthase.
- Irreversibly blocks dTMP synthesis, halting DNA replication.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In the de novo synthesis of pyrimidines, the atoms of the completed pyrimidine ring are donated by Glutamine, CO2, and [___].
back:
Aspartic Acid (Aspartate).
- Contributes three carbons and one nitrogen to the six-membered ring.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A child presents with high urinary orotic acid levels. What clinical finding differentiates Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency from UMP Synthase deficiency?
back:
Hyperammonemia.
- OTC deficiency (Urea Cycle) causes elevated blood ammonia.
- UMP Synthase deficiency (Pyrimidine pathway) presents with megaloblastic anemia but normal ammonia levels.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain how oral Uridine administration resolves the metabolic crisis in hereditary Orotic Aciduria.
back:
- Uridine is salvaged by nucleoside kinases to UMP.
- This bypasses the enzymatic block in the de novo pathway.
- UTP (produced from UMP) feedback-inhibits CPS II, reducing orotic acid overproduction.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the assembly order of the nitrogenous ring between the de novo purine and pyrimidine pathways.
back:
- Purine: Ring is built directly atom-by-atom onto a pre-existing Ribose-5-Phosphate.
- Pyrimidine: The ring (Orotate) is synthesized completely first, then attached to Ribose-5-Phosphate (PRPP).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: List the final soluble metabolic products of the degradation of Uracil and Cytosine in humans.
back:
- Beta-alanine.
- Carbon Dioxide (CO2).
- Ammonia (NH3).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In mammalian de novo pyrimidine synthesis, the primary regulated step is the production of carbamoyl phosphate catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back:
Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
- Located in the cytosol.
- Inhibited by UTP (feedback inhibition).
- Activated by PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia that does not respond to Vitamin B12 or folate, along with growth retardation and high urinary orotic acid. Identify the deficient enzyme.
back:
UMP Synthase.
- Bifunctional enzyme with orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase domains.
- Causes Hereditary Orotic Aciduria.
- Treated with oral uridine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) inhibits pyrimidine nucleotide production.
back:
Suicide Inhibition.
- Converted to 5-FdUMP.
- Permanently binds and inactivates Thymidylate Synthase.
- Depletes dTMP, halting DNA synthesis and cell proliferation.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: CPS I vs CPS II Isoenzymes
front: Contrast Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II) regarding their cellular location and nitrogen source.
back:
CPS I: Mitochondria; uses Ammonia (NH3) as nitrogen source (Urea Cycle).
- CPS II: Cytosol; uses Glutamine as nitrogen source (Pyrimidine synthesis).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the three specific precursors that contribute all atoms to the pyrimidine ring structure.
back:
Aspartic Acid (provides C4, C5, C6, and N1).
- Glutamine (provides N3).
- Carbon Dioxide/Bicarbonate (provides C2).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The only enzyme of the pyrimidine de novo pathway that is not cytosolic and is instead located on the inner mitochondrial membrane is [___].
back:
Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase.
- Oxidizes dihydroorotate to orotate.
- Utilizes FAD as a cofactor.
- Linked to the electron transport chain.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A neonate with hyperammonemia due to Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency also shows significant orotic aciduria. Relate this to pyrimidine metabolism.
back:
Mitochondrial Carbamoyl Phosphate accumulates.
- Leaks into the cytosol.
- Overloads the pyrimidine pathway, bypassing the regulated CPS II step.
- Results in excessive orotic acid production.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the unique dual role of N5, N10-Methylene Tetrahydrofolate in the conversion of dUMP to dTMP.
back:
One-carbon donor: Provides the methyl group.
- Reducing agent: Provides two hydrogen atoms.
- Result: THF is oxidized to Dihydrofolate (DHF).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the order of ring assembly and ribose attachment in de novo purine versus pyrimidine synthesis.
back:
Purines: Ring is built directly onto Ribose-5-Phosphate.
- Pyrimidines: Nitrogenous ring (Orotate) is fully synthesized first, then attached to PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the final, highly soluble end products of pyrimidine ring catabolism in humans.
back:
Beta-alanine (from Uracil/Cytosine).
- Beta-aminoisobutyrate (from Thymine).
- NH3 and CO2.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The committed and rate-limiting step of de novo pyrimidine synthesis in human cytosolic cells is catalyzed by [___].
back:
Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
- Inhibited by UTP (end-product inhibition).
- Activated by PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia, poor growth, and orotic acid crystals in the urine. Despite B12 and folate therapy, the anemia persists. Identify the likely defective enzyme.
back:
UMP Synthase.
- A bifunctional enzyme with Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase activities.
- Deficiency causes Hereditary Orotic Aciduria.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the dual role of Phosphoribosyl Pyrophosphate (PRPP) in the de novo pyrimidine biosynthetic pathway.
back:
- Allosteric activator of CPS II (the rate-limiting enzyme).
- Essential substrate (ribose-5-phosphate donor) for converting orotate to Orotidine 5'-monophosphate (OMP).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the lab findings of Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency with UMP Synthase deficiency regarding nitrogen metabolism.
back:
OTC Deficiency: Orotic aciduria PLUS hyperammonemia (urea cycle defect).
UMP Synthase Deficiency: Orotic aciduria WITHOUT hyperammonemia; presents with megaloblastic anemia.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the three specific molecular precursors that contribute atoms to the construction of the pyrimidine ring.
back:
- Glutamine (amide nitrogen).
- Aspartate (C4, C5, C6, and N1).
- CO2 (C2 carbon).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The enzyme thymidylate synthase is irreversibly inhibited by the 'suicide inhibitor' 5-FdUMP, which is the active metabolite of the drug [___].
back:
5-Fluorouracil (5-FU).
- Halts DNA synthesis by preventing dTMP production.
- Used as an antineoplastic agent.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient on Methotrexate therapy shows decreased levels of dTMP. Explain the indirect mechanism of this inhibition on pyrimidine synthesis.
back:
Methotrexate inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase.
- Depletes Tetrahydrofolate (THF).
- Limits N5,N10-methylene THF, the essential methyl donor for Thymidylate Synthase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the unique cellular localization and cofactor requirement of Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase.
back:
- Located on the inner mitochondrial membrane (unlike all other cytosolic pyrimidine enzymes).
- Requires FAD as a cofactor to oxidize dihydroorotate to orotic acid.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the end products of purine degradation with those of pyrimidine degradation regarding clinical toxicity.
back:
Purine degradation: Uric acid (relatively insoluble; can lead to Gout/Urolithiasis).
Pyrimidine degradation: Beta-alanine and Beta-aminoisobutyrate (highly soluble; nontoxic).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Why is oral Uridine the treatment of choice for patients with Hereditary Orotic Aciduria?
back:
- Salvaged by uridine kinase to UMP, bypassing the enzymatic block.
- UMP (and subsequent UTP) provides feedback inhibition of CPS II, reducing orotic acid production.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting step of de-novo pyrimidine synthesis in human cells is catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back:
Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS-II).
- Located in the cytosol.
- Inhibited by UTP (feedback inhibition).
- Activated by PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia unresponsive to B12/Folate, poor growth, and high urinary orotic acid. Identify the deficient enzyme.
back:
UMP Synthase deficiency (Hereditary Orotic Aciduria).
- Affects orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase domains.
- Treatment: Oral Uridine to bypass the metabolic block.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the anti-neoplastic mechanism of 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) within the pyrimidine pathway.
back:
Suicide Inhibition of Thymidylate Synthase.
- Converted to 5-FdUMP.
- Irreversibly binds the enzyme.
- Prevents conversion of dUMP to dTMP, halting DNA synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast the cause of Orotic Aciduria in UMP Synthase deficiency versus Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency.
back:
- UMP Synthase: Direct block in pyrimidine synthesis; normal ammonia levels.
- OTC Deficiency: Urea cycle defect; excess mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate leaks into cytosol, stimulating orotate production; presents with hyperammonemia.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the three primary molecular precursors required for the de-novo assembly of the pyrimidine ring.
back:
- Glutamine (provides amide nitrogen).
- CO2 (provides carbon).
- Aspartic Acid (provides the remaining ring atoms).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Unlike purines which produce uric acid, pyrimidine ring catabolism yields highly soluble end-products such as [___].
back:
Beta-alanine and Beta-aminoisobutyrate.
- The pyrimidine ring is opened/cleaved during degradation.
- Also produces CO2 and NH3.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient with Hereditary Orotic Aciduria is administered Uridine. Explain the biochemical rationale for using a salvage pathway component as treatment.
back:
Salvage pathway utilization.
- Uridine is converted to UMP by uridine kinase.
- Bypasses the UMP synthase block.
- Resynthesized UTP provides feedback inhibition of CPS-II, reducing orotate production.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Role of DHFR in Nucleotide Synthesis
front: Describe the role of Dihydrofolate Reductase (DHFR) in maintaining the flow of thymidine monophosphate (dTMP) synthesis.
back:
Regeneration of Tetrahydrofolate (THF).
- Thymidylate synthase oxidizes methylene-THF to Dihydrofolate (DHF).
- DHFR reduces DHF back to THF.
- Inhibition (e.g., by Methotrexate) depletes THF, stopping dTMP production.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Contrast Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS-I) with Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS-II) regarding location and nitrogen source.
back:
- CPS-I: Mitochondria; Urea cycle; Uses Ammonia (NH3).
- CPS-II: Cytosol; Pyrimidine synthesis; Uses Glutamine.
- CPS-I requires N-acetylglutamate; CPS-II is inhibited by UTP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the parent pyrimidine nucleotide from which all other pyrimidine nucleotides are derived.
back:
Uridine Monophosphate (UMP).
- Formed from OMP via decarboxylation.
- Phosphorylated to UDP/UTP.
- UTP is then aminated to CTP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The de-novo synthesis of pyrimidines begins with the formation of carbamoyl phosphate from CO2 and the amino acid [___].
back:
• Glutamine (provides the amide nitrogen).
• Aspartate (provides most of the ring atoms).
• Occurs in the cytosol.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia unresponsive to B12/Folate therapy and white crystalluria. Identify the deficient enzyme and the recommended treatment.
back:
• UMP Synthase (bifunctional enzyme deficiency).
• Results in Hereditary Orotic Aciduria.
• Treatment: Oral Uridine (bypasses the block).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the allosteric regulation of Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II) in pyrimidine biosynthesis.
back:
• Inhibitor: UTP (feedback inhibition).
• Activator: PRPP (feed-forward activation).
• This is the rate-limiting step.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: CPS I vs CPS II Isoenzymes
front: Contrast the cellular localization and nitrogen source between CPS I and CPS II.
back:
• CPS I: Mitochondria; uses Ammonia; (Urea Cycle).
• CPS II: Cytosol; uses Glutamine; (Pyrimidine Synthesis).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Describe the structural organization of the 'CAD' multifunctional polypeptide in pyrimidine synthesis.
back:
• Single protein with three domains.
• Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II.
• Aspartate transcarbamoylase.
• Dihydroorotase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Unlike the insoluble uric acid of purine catabolism, pyrimidine degradation results in the highly soluble products [___] and [___].
back:
• ̢-Alanine (from uracil/cytosine).
• ̢-Aminoisobutyrate (from thymine).
• Both are excreted easily in urine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A patient with Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency shows elevated orotic acid in the urine. Why does a Urea Cycle defect stimulate pyrimidine synthesis?
back:
• Mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate accumulates.
• Leaks into the cytosol.
• Overwhelms CPS II and enters pyrimidine pathway.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the biological importance of dUTPase (UTP diphosphatase) in pyrimidine metabolism.
back:
• Hydrolyzes dUTP to dUMP.
• Prevents high dUTP levels.
• Reduces erroneous uracil incorporation into DNA.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish between de-novo purine and pyrimidine synthesis regarding the timing of Ribose-5-Phosphate (PRPP) addition.
back:
• Purine: Built directly onto the PRPP.
• Pyrimidine: Ring synthesized first (Orotate), then attached to PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Name the enzyme inhibited by 5-Fluorouracil and its specific therapeutic outcome.
back:
• Thymidylate Synthase.
• Blocked conversion: dUMP → dTMP.
• Inhibits DNA synthesis/cell proliferation.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: In the de-novo synthesis of purines, the amino acid that provides the nitrogen group for the conversion of Inosine Monophosphate (IMP) to Adenylosuccinate is [___].
back: Aspartate (also used in the synthesis of the purine ring at an earlier step).

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: A transplant recipient experiences decreased T and B cell proliferation while on Mycophenolic acid. This drug achieves immunosuppression by inhibiting the conversion of [___] to [___].
back: Inosine Monophosphate (IMP) to Xanthosine Monophosphate (XMP) by inhibiting IMP Dehydrogenase.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: Explain how the cell utilizes reciprocal energy requirements to balance the production of Adenosine and Guanosine nucleotides.
back:
• AMP synthesis requires GTP as an energy source.
• GMP synthesis requires ATP as an energy source.
• This prevents the overproduction of one purine when the other is deficient.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: Distinguish between the conversion of IMP to AMP versus IMP to GMP regarding the intermediate molecules and nitrogen donors used.
back:
• IMP to AMP: Intermediate is Adenylosuccinate; uses Aspartate as N-donor.
• IMP to GMP: Intermediate is Xanthosine Monophosphate (XMP); uses Glutamine as N-donor.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: Identify the primary regulatory mechanism that prevents de-novo purine synthesis when both AMP and GMP levels are high.
back: Feedback inhibition of the committed step (PRPP Amidotransferase) and specific inhibition of the first reaction in each IMP-branching pathway.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: The enzyme required to convert Guanosine Monophosphate (GMP) to Guanosine Diphosphate (GDP) using ATP as the phosphate donor is [___].
back: Guanylate Kinase (a base-specific nucleoside monophosphate kinase).

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: A skeletal muscle biopsy during high-intensity exercise shows high levels of AMP. Identify the enzyme that maintains the ATP/ADP/AMP equilibrium in this tissue.
back: Adenylate Kinase (Myokinase); it catalyzes the reaction: 2 ADP ↔ ATP + AMP.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: Describe the final step required to synthesize a purine nucleoside triphosphate from its corresponding diphosphate form.
back:
• Enzyme: Nucleoside Diphosphate Kinase.
• Mechanism: Transfers a phosphate from ATP to any NDP (e.g., GDP to GTP).
• Feature: It has broad specificity for both ribose and deoxyribose sugars.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: Contrast the redox requirements of the IMP-to-AMP branch versus the IMP-to-GMP branch.
back:
• IMP-to-AMP: Does not require redox cofactors.
• IMP-to-GMP: Requires NAD+ for the oxidation of IMP to XMP by IMP Dehydrogenase.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: Name the TCA cycle intermediate released when Adenylosuccinate is cleaved to form AMP.
back: Fumarate (catalyzed by the enzyme Adenylosuccinate Lyase/Adenylosuccinase).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The rate-limiting and regulated step of de-novo pyrimidine synthesis in humans is catalyzed by the cytosolic enzyme [___].
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
• Activated by: PRPP.
• Inhibited by: UTP (feedback inhibition).
• Uses: Glutamine and CO2 as substrates.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A child presents with megaloblastic anemia and growth retardation. Labs show high urinary orotic acid but normal blood ammonia. Identify the likely defective bifunctional enzyme.
back:
• UMP Synthase.
• Defective domains: Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase.
• Management: Administration of Uridine (bypasses the metabolic block).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which dUMP is converted to dTMP during DNA synthesis.
back:
• Enzyme: Thymidylate synthase.
• Cofactor: N5, N10-Methylene tetrahydrofolate (THF).
• Process: Transfers a methyl group and reduces THF to DHF.
• Clinical: Target for 5-Fluorouracil.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: CPS I vs CPS II Differential
front: Contrast Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and II (CPS II) regarding their cellular location and primary metabolic role.
back:
• CPS I: Mitochondria; involved in Urea Cycle; utilizes Ammonia.
• CPS II: Cytosol; involved in Pyrimidine Synthesis; utilizes Glutamine nitrogen.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the enzyme inhibited by 5-Fluorouracil and its specific classification as a pharmacological inhibitor.
back:
• Enzyme: Thymidylate synthase.
• Type: Suicide inhibitor (permanently binds the enzyme).
• Effect: Depletes dTMP, halting DNA synthesis and cell division.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: The three primary molecular precursors that contribute atoms to the pyrimidine ring are CO2, Glutamine, and [___].
back:
• Aspartic Acid (Aspartate).
• Aspartate contributes C4, C5, C6, and N1 atoms to the ring structure.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A neonate with hyperammonemia exhibits increased orotic acid in the urine. Explain why a urea cycle defect causes this pyrimidine-related finding.
back:
• Diagnosis: Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency.
• Pathophysiology: Excess mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate leaks into the cytosol.
• Mechanism: It overloads the pyrimidine pathway, bypassing regulated CPS II.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Detail the end products of pyrimidine catabolism and contrast their clinical significance with purine end products.
back:
• Products: CO2, NH3, β-alanine, and β-aminoisobutyrate.
• Solubility: Highly water-soluble.
• Contrast: Unlike purine degradation (uric acid), pyrimidine products do not cause gout or stones.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Distinguish between de-novo pyrimidine and purine synthesis regarding the assembly of the nitrogenous ring onto the ribose sugar.
back:
• Purines: Ring is built directly on ribose-5-phosphate (PRPP).
• Pyrimidines: Ring (Orotic acid) is completed first and then attached to PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Role of PRPP in Pyrimidine Metabolism
front: Name the activated pentose that serves as the ribose 5-phosphate donor for both pyrimidine de-novo and salvage pathways.
back:
• 5-Phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP).
• Function: Essential for converting Orotic acid to OMP via Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: In the specific pathway converting Inosine Monophosphate (IMP) to Adenylosuccinate, the required source of energy is [___].
back:
GTP (Guanosine Triphosphate).
- Provides the energy for the addition of aspartate to IMP.
- Facilitates reciprocal regulation of purine levels.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: A transplant patient receives Mycophenolic acid to prevent graft rejection. This drug acts by inhibiting the enzyme [___], thereby depleting GMP pools in T and B cells.
back:
IMP Dehydrogenase.
- Reversibly inhibits the conversion of IMP to XMP.
- Specifically deprives proliferating lymphocytes of essential guanine nucleotides.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: Explain the biological logic behind the 'cross-regulation' mechanism where GTP is used for AMP synthesis and ATP is used for GMP synthesis.
back:
Ensures balanced production:
- High GTP levels drive AMP synthesis.
- High ATP levels drive GMP synthesis.
- Prevents overproduction of one purine species relative to the other.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: Contrast the nitrogen donors and the byproducts released during the conversion of IMP to AMP versus IMP to GMP.
back:
IMP to AMP:
- Donor: Aspartate.
- Byproduct: Fumarate.
IMP to GMP:
- Donor: Glutamine (amide group).
- Byproduct: Glutamate.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: Identify the carbon-skeleton byproduct released by Adenylosuccinate Lyase during the final step of AMP production.
back:
Fumarate.
- Released when Adenylosuccinate is cleaved to Adenosine Monophosphate (AMP).
- Can subsequently enter the TCA cycle.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: The immediate intermediate formed by the NAD+-dependent oxidation of Inosine Monophosphate (IMP) is [___].
back:
Xanthosine Monophosphate (XMP).
- Catalyzed by IMP Dehydrogenase.
- XMP is subsequently aminated to form GMP.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: A laboratory study finds that high concentrations of GMP inhibit the first step of its own synthesis from IMP. Identify the enzyme targeted by this feedback inhibition.
back:
IMP Dehydrogenase.
- GMP acts as an allosteric inhibitor.
- This is the committed step for the GMP branch of the pathway.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: Describe the specific equilibrium reaction catalyzed by Adenylate Kinase in muscle tissue during high energy demand.
back:
AMP + ATP ↔ 2 ADP.
- Maintains equilibrium between adenine nucleotides.
- Crucial for recycling AMP back into the energy pool.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: Distinguish between the substrate specificities of Nucleoside Monophosphate Kinases and Nucleoside Diphosphate Kinases.
back:
Monophosphate Kinases:
- Highly specific for the base (e.g., Adenylate kinase, Guanylate kinase).
- Do not distinguish between ribose/deoxyribose.
Diphosphate Kinases:
- Broad specificity for all NDPs and NTPs.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
front: Identify the primary source of the high-energy phosphate used to convert GDP and ADP into their respective triphosphates (GTP/ATP).
back:
ATP.
- ATP is the universal phosphate donor due to its higher cellular concentration.
- Catalyzed by Nucleoside Diphosphate Kinase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: In the de novo synthesis of pyrimidines, the regulated and rate-limiting step is the production of [___] from glutamine and CO2.
back: • Carbamoyl phosphate • Produced by CPS II (the regulated step) • Allosterically activated by PRPP and inhibited by UTP • Distinct from CPS I used in urea synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: A 1-year-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia, poor growth, and high urinary orotic acid, but normal blood ammonia. State the most likely diagnosis.
back: • UMP Synthase deficiency (Hereditary Orotic Aciduria) • Leads to megaloblastic anemia and growth failure • Characterized by excessive urinary orotate and normal ammonia • Managed with exogenous uridine supplementation.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Explain the biochemical role of N5,N10-methylene tetrahydrofolate in the synthesis of Thymidine monophosphate (dTMP).
back: • Acts as a methyl donor for dUMP • Provides two hydrogen atoms for reduction • Oxidized to Dihydrofolate (DHF) by Thymidylate Synthase • Essential component for DNA replication.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: CPS I vs CPS II Comparison
front: Contrast Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I) and CPS II regarding their cellular location and nitrogen source.
back: • CPS I: Located in mitochondria, uses Ammonia, part of Urea Cycle • CPS II: Located in cytosol, uses Glutamine, part of Pyrimidine Synthesis • Only CPS II is activated by PRPP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
front: Identify the three distinct catalytic domains found in the single cytosolic polypeptide known as CAD.
back: • Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II • Aspartate transcarbamoylase • Dihydroorotase • This tri-functional polypeptide organizes the first three steps of cytosolic pyrimidine synthesis to improve metabolic efficiency.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
