• Accompanied by neurological symptoms like choreoathetosis.
• Distinguishes LNS from other causes of pediatric hyperuricemia.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: A young male with HGPRT deficiency develops painful joint swelling and kidney stones. Name the specific degradation product and explain why it accumulates.
back:
Monosodium urate (Uric Acid):
• HGPRT deficiency prevents recycling of purines.
• Excessive de novo synthesis creates a purine surplus.
• Surplus is catabolized to insoluble uric acid, causing gout and stones.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Differentiate between the pediatric renal stones found in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome and those found in Hereditary Orotic Aciduria.
back:
Differential Stone Analysis:
• Lesch-Nyhan: Urate stones; result from excessive purine degradation.
• Orotic Aciduria: Orotic acid stones; result from a pyrimidine synthesis block (UMP synthase deficiency).
• Only Lesch-Nyhan features neurological self-mutilation.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Distinguish between the fate of PRPP in the Purine Salvage loop versus the De Novo synthesis loop.
back:
Metabolic Loop Contrast:
• Salvage Loop: PRPP reacts with free bases to directly form nucleotides (IMP/GMP).
• De Novo Loop: PRPP is the initial scaffold for stepwise ring construction.
• Salvage is more energy-efficient than de novo.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: State the inheritance pattern of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome and identify the gender predominantly affected.
back:
X-linked recessive inheritance:
• Primarily affects males.
• Females are typically asymptomatic carriers.
• Caused by mutations in the HPRT1 gene on the X chromosome.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is an X-linked recessive disorder characterized by a virtually complete deficiency of the enzyme [___].
back:
• HGPRT (Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase).
• Failure of this enzyme prevents the salvage of hypoxanthine and guanine, leading to hyperuricemia.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: A 2-year-old boy presents with cognitive deficits, spasticity, and severe self-mutilation, including biting his lips and fingers. His mother notes orange-colored crystals in his diaper. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome.
• The "orange sand" in diapers represents sodium urate crystals, indicating extreme hyperuricemia.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Explain the mechanism by which HGPRT deficiency leads to the massive overproduction of purines de novo.
back:
• Loss of salvage causes PRPP accumulation (substrate for de novo synthesis).
• Decreased levels of IMP and GMP remove feedback inhibition on Glutamine:PRPP amidotransferase.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Contrast the typical joint involvement in a 5-year-old Lesch-Nyhan patient with that of an adult suffering from idiopathic gout.
back:
• Lesch-Nyhan: Early-onset gouty arthritis and tophi due to hereditary enzyme deficiency.
• Idiopathic Gout: Usually presents in middle-aged adults due to underexcretion or diet.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Assess the efficacy of Allopurinol in managing the neurological and behavioral symptoms of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
back:
• Allopurinol is ineffective for neurological symptoms.
• It reduces uric acid/gout symptoms only.
• Neurological deficits are likely due to brain dependence on the salvage pathway.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: In the laboratory diagnosis of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, the serum levels of [___] are found to be characteristically elevated.
back:
• Uric Acid.
• Secondary findings include elevated PRPP levels and decreased HGPRT activity in cell lysates.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: A male infant presents with involuntary movements and self-biting. If the biochemical cause is an inability to recycle hypoxanthine, name the required co-substrate that accumulates in excess.
back:
• PRPP (5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate).
• Its accumulation is a major driver of the accelerated de novo purine pathway.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Why does the brain exhibit more severe symptoms in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome compared to other tissues like the liver?
back:
• The brain has extremely low levels of de novo purine synthesis enzymes.
• It is uniquely reliant on the HGPRT-mediated salvage pathway for its nucleotide pool.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Contrast the metabolic fate of Hypoxanthine in a healthy individual versus a patient with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
back:
• Healthy: Salvaged to IMP via HGPRT.
• Lesch-Nyhan: Obligatorily oxidized to Xanthine and then Uric Acid by Xanthine Oxidase.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Identify the inheritance pattern and the gender predominantly affected by Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
back:
• X-linked Recessive.
• Predominantly affects males; females are typically asymptomatic carriers unless X-inactivation is skewed.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: In a pediatric patient presenting with Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID), the autosomal recessive deficiency of the enzyme [___] leads to a toxic accumulation of dATP within lymphocytes.
back:
Adenosine Deaminase (ADA)
* Prevents DNA synthesis and cell division.
* Leads to T, B, and NK cell depletion.
* Causes profound lymphopenia and recurrent infections.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 50-year-old male presents with sudden, excruciating pain in the first metatarsophalangeal joint after a seafood dinner. Synovial fluid analysis reveals needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals. State the most likely diagnosis.
back:
Acute Gouty Arthritis
* Triggered by high-purine diets (seafood/meat).
* Caused by monosodium urate crystal deposition.
* Associated with hyperuricemia.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency specifically arrests the proliferation of T and B lymphocytes.
back:
* Accumulation of deoxyadenosine increases dATP levels.
* High dATP allosterically inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase.
* This prevents the production of all deoxyribonucleotides.
* DNA synthesis and lymphocyte division cease.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the pharmacological targets and indications for Allopurinol versus Probenecid in managing chronic hyperuricemia.
back:
* Allopurinol: Inhibits Xanthine Oxidase; reduces uric acid production.
* Probenecid: Uricosuric agent; increases renal excretion via OAT transporters.
* Allopurinol is preferred for overproducers; Probenecid for underexcretors.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Describe the specific action of Colchicine that makes it effective in treating acute gouty inflammation despite having no effect on uric acid levels.
back:
* Binds to tubulin, inhibiting microtubule polymerization.
* Impairs neutrophil chemotaxis and phagocytosis.
* Reduces the inflammatory response to urate crystals.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: To confirm a diagnosis of gout, aspirated synovial fluid must show monosodium urate crystals that appear [___] under polarized light and exhibit [___] birefringence.
back:
Needle-shaped; Negative
* Yellow when parallel to the slow wave.
* Blue when perpendicular.
* Key diagnostic differentiator from pseudogout.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 4-month-old infant presents with oral candidiasis, chronic diarrhea, and failure to thrive. Lab data reveals a lack of thymic shadow and lymphopenia. If this results from purine degradation failure, identify the enzyme.
back:
Adenosine Deaminase (ADA)
* Deficiency causes 14% of SCID cases.
* Treated with BMT, ERT, or gene therapy.
* Results in developmental arrest of lymphocytes.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Outline the two-step oxidative process catalyzed by Xanthine Oxidase to produce the final metabolic byproduct of human purine catabolism.
back:
* Step 1: Oxidizes Hypoxanthine to Xanthine.
* Step 2: Oxidizes Xanthine to Uric Acid.
* Uses molecular oxygen and generates hydrogen peroxide.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Distinguish between 'overproduction' and 'underexcretion' as causes of secondary hyperuricemia.
back:
* Overproduction: High cell turnover (leukemia, chemotherapy, psoriasis).
* Underexcretion: Renal failure, thiazide diuretics, or lactic acidosis (competition for excretion).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Identify the X-linked recessive disorder where a virtually complete deficiency of HGPRT causes uric acid stones, gouty arthritis, and compulsive self-mutilation.
back:
Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome
* Failure to salvage hypoxanthine or guanine.
* Results in increased PRPP and de novo synthesis.
* Characterized by hyperuricemia and motor dysfunction.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is a rare, X-linked recessive disorder caused by a virtually complete deficiency of the enzyme [___].
back:
• Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT).
• Leads to inability to salvage hypoxanthine or guanine.
• Results in massive overproduction of uric acid.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: A 2-year-old male presents with orange-colored 'sand' in his diaper, swollen joints, and missing tissue on his lower lip. Identify the pathophysiology behind these findings.
back:
• HGPRT deficiency causes hyperuricemia.
• Uric acid crystals (sodium urate) deposit in joints/kidneys.
• Neurological dysfunction leads to characteristic self-mutilation behaviors.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Explain the role of Phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate (PRPP) accumulation in the metabolic progression of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
back:
• PRPP is a substrate for HGPRT salvage.
• Absence of HGPRT prevents PRPP utilization.
• Accumulating PRPP allosterically activates the committed step of de novo purine synthesis.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Distinguish the laboratory biochemical profile of a patient with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome from a patient with primary idiopathic gout regarding enzyme levels.
back:
• Lesch-Nyhan: HGPRT activity <1-2% of normal.
• Idiopathic Gout: HGPRT levels typically normal; usually due to renal underexcretion (~90%).
• Lesch-Nyhan presents with severe cognitive/motor deficits.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Describe the pharmacological mechanism of Allopurinol in managing the biochemical abnormalities of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
back:
• Structural analog of hypoxanthine.
• Competitively inhibits Xanthine Oxidase.
• Accumulates hypoxanthine/xanthine (more soluble than uric acid).
• Reduces risk of urolithiasis and gouty arthritis.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: The characteristic behavioral hallmark of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome involving compulsive biting of fingers and lips is termed [___].
back:
• Self-mutilation.
• Likely related to neurotransmitter imbalances (dopamine) in the basal ganglia.
• Distinct from simple cognitive delay.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
coreConcept: Loss of Feedback Inhibition in LN
front: A pediatric patient with hyperuricemia shows significantly decreased intracellular levels of IMP and GMP. Relate this finding to the regulation of de novo purine synthesis.
back:
• IMP and GMP are feedback inhibitors of the committed step.
• Low levels remove inhibition of Glutamine:PRPP amidotransferase.
• Leads to uncontrolled de novo purine overproduction.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Analyze how the failure of the purine salvage pathway in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome creates a 'double stimulus' for de novo purine biosynthesis.
back:
• Stimulus 1: High levels of substrate PRPP (activator).
• Stimulus 2: Low levels of IMP/GMP (inhibitors missing).
• Result: Massive upregulation of Glutamine:PRPP amidotransferase.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Contrast the cause of hyperuricemia in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome with the hyperuricemia seen in Von Gierke disease (G6Pase deficiency).
back:
• Lesch-Nyhan: Failure of salvage and loss of feedback inhibition.
• Von Gierke: G6P shunted to Pentose Phosphate Pathway, overproducing ribose-5-P and PRPP.
• Both result in purine overproduction.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
front: Identify the primary end product of purine catabolism that is responsible for the formation of 'orange sand' in the urine of Lesch-Nyhan patients.
back:
• Uric acid (excreted as sodium urate).
• High turnover of purines due to de novo overproduction.
• Leads to urolithiasis and potential renal failure.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: In the biochemical pathogenesis of gout, the deposition of [___] crystals in the synovial fluid triggers an acute inflammatory response in the joints.
back:
• Monosodium urate (MSU)
• Needle-shaped morphology
• Negatively birefringent under polarized light microscopy

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 50-year-old male presents with sudden, excruciating pain in the first metatarsophalangeal joint (podagra). Serum urate is 9.5 mg/dL. Specify the definitive diagnostic finding.
back:
• Arthrocentesis (joint aspiration)
• Needle-shaped crystals within synovial fluid
• Negative birefringence under polarized light

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain how an inherited deficiency of Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) leads to the massive depletion of T and B lymphocytes in SCID.
back:
• Adenosine and dATP accumulate
• dATP inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase
• DNA synthesis/cell division is blocked
• Lymphocyte apoptosis is triggered

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the underlying metabolic cause of hyperuricemia in patients with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome versus those with renal underexcretion.
back:
• Lesch-Nyhan: HGPRT deficiency leads to increased PRPP and de novo purine overproduction
• Underexcretion: Inherent renal defects or diuretics reducing urate clearance

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Specify the pharmacological mechanism of Allopurinol in the long-term management of hyperuricemia.
back:
• Structural analog of hypoxanthine
• Competitive inhibitor of Xanthine Oxidase
• Decreases conversion of xanthine to uric acid

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID) caused by ADA deficiency is characterized by the systemic depletion of [___], [___], and [___] cells.
back:
• T-lymphocytes
• B-lymphocytes
• Natural Killer (NK) cells

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 4-month-old infant presents with recurrent pneumonia, oral candidiasis, and persistent diarrhea. Lab data shows a near-total absence of serum immunoglobulins and lymphopenia. Identify the likely enzyme defect.
back:
• Adenosine Deaminase (ADA)
• Results in autosomal recessive SCID
• Death usually occurs by age 2 without treatment

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Detail the role of PRPP Synthetase mutations in causing primary gouty overproduction.
back:
• Mutations increase Vmax or decrease feedback sensitivity
• Excessive PRPP activates the committed step of purine synthesis
• Accelerates catabolism to uric acid

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Distinguish between the therapeutic indications and actions of Colchicine and Probenecid.
back:
• Colchicine: Acute flare; inhibits microtubule assembly to decrease neutrophil migration
• Probenecid: Chronic prophylaxis; uricosuric that increases renal urate excretion

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Identify the relatively insoluble end product of human purine catabolism that precipitates in joints and kidneys.
back:
• Uric Acid
• Normal end product in humans (primates lack urate oxidase)
• Precipitates at high concentrations as monosodium urate

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: In patients with suspected gouty arthritis, a definitive diagnosis is confirmed by identifying [___] crystals under polarized light microscopy of synovial fluid.
back:
• Negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals.
• Composed of Monosodium Urate (MSU).
• Often found within polymorphonuclear leukocytes during acute attacks.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 52-year-old male presents with excruciating pain in his right big toe (podagra) following a seafood dinner. Explain the biochemical basis for why dietary purines trigger this condition.
back:
• Dietary purines are degraded to uric acid in intestinal mucosal cells.
• Uric acid enters the blood, raising plasma levels.
• When levels exceed saturation, urate crystals deposit in joints, triggering inflammation.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency leads to the failure of DNA synthesis in lymphocytes.
back:
• ADA deficiency causes accumulation of dATP.
• High dATP levels allosterically inhibit Ribonucleotide Reductase.
• This prevents the formation of all deoxyribonucleotides (dNTPs).
• Lack of dNTPs halts DNA replication and triggers lymphocyte apoptosis.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A patient with chronic gout is found to have a mutation in the PRPP Synthetase gene. Contrast the 'Overproduction' vs 'Underexcretion' types of hyperuricemia regarding their primary renal handling.
back:
• Overproduction: Increased purine synthesis (e.g., PRPP Synthetase mutation) overloads renal capacity.
• Underexcretion: Primary defect in renal transporters (e.g., competition with lactate or thiazides).
• Result: Both lead to monosodium urate crystal deposition.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Describe the pharmacological activation and primary molecular target of Allopurinol in the treatment of chronic gout.
back:
• Activation: Converted to oxypurinol (alloxanthine) in the body.
• Mechanism: Acts as a suicide inhibitor of Xanthine Oxidase.
• Effect: Reduces the production of uric acid by stopping hypoxanthine/xanthine oxidation.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: In the context of purine degradation, the final product excreted in human urine is [___], which is relatively insoluble in its ionized form.
back:
• Uric Acid.
• Produced by the enzyme Xanthine Oxidase.
• Levels close to saturation in blood increase risk for crystallization.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 4-month-old male presents with recurrent thrush, failure to thrive, and severe lymphopenia (absent T and B cells). What is the most likely metabolic diagnosis, and what imaging finding is characteristic?
back:
• Diagnosis: SCID due to Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency.
• Characteristic Finding: Absent thymic shadow on chest X-ray.
• Labs: Profound depletion of T, B, and NK cells.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Detail the specific kinetic changes in the PRPP Synthetase enzyme that result in the overproduction of purines in certain gout patients.
back:
• Increased Vmax for producing PRPP.
• Decreased Km for the substrate Ribose 5-phosphate.
• Resistance to feedback inhibition by purine nucleotides (AMP/GMP).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the immunological impact of Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency with Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency.
back:
• ADA Deficiency: Affects T, B, and NK cells (Severe Combined Immunodeficiency).
• PNP Deficiency: Primarily affects T-cells.
• Severity: ADA deficiency is generally more severe and leads to earlier mortality if untreated.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
coreConcept: Secondary Gout in Glycogen Storage Disease
front: Explain why patients with Von Gierke disease often suffer from secondary gout.
back:
• Increased Glucose 6-phosphate enters the Pentose Phosphate Pathway.
• This leads to overproduction of Ribose 5-phosphate and PRPP.
• Elevated PRPP stimulates de novo purine synthesis.
• Simultaneous lactic acidosis causes renal underexcretion of urate.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: In patients with acute gouty arthritis, synovial fluid analysis under polarized light microscopy reveals needle-shaped crystals that exhibit [___] birefringence.
back:
• Negative birefringence.
• Crystals appear yellow when parallel to the slow axis.
• Composed of monosodium urate.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 55-year-old male with leukemia develops severe big toe pain following the initiation of chemotherapy. Explain the metabolic basis for this sudden joint inflammation.
back:
• High cell turnover (Tumor Lysis Syndrome) increases nucleic acid breakdown.
• Purines are catabolized into uric acid.
• Hyperuricemia leads to monosodium urate crystal deposition in joints.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Describe the biochemical mechanism by which Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency results in the depletion of T, B, and NK cells.
back:
• Adenosine and deoxyadenosine accumulate.
• Deoxyadenosine is phosphorylated to dATP.
• High dATP inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase.
• DNA synthesis is halted, causing lymphocyte apoptosis.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the clinical presentation of orotic aciduria caused by UMP Synthase deficiency with that caused by Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency.
back:
• UMP Synthase: Megaloblastic anemia; normal blood ammonia.
• OTC Deficiency: No megaloblastic anemia; hyperammonemia present.
• Both present with elevated urinary orotic acid.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: State the pharmacological mechanism of Allopurinol and its active metabolite in treating chronic gout.
back:
• Structural analog of hypoxanthine.
• Competitively inhibits Xanthine Oxidase.
• Metabolized to oxypurinol (alloxanthine).
• Reduces production of insoluble uric acid.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: The autosomal recessive disorder characterized by the absence of [___] results in a less severe form of SCID that primarily affects T-cell function.
back:
• Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase (PNP).
• Results in accumulation of dGTP.
• Less common than ADA deficiency.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 1-year-old child presents with recurrent fungal, viral, and bacterial infections, and a chest X-ray reveals the absence of a thymic shadow. Identify the most likely enzyme deficiency.
back:
• Adenosine Deaminase (ADA).
• Leads to Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID).
• Characterized by lymphocytopenia and failure to thrive.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Distinguish between the mechanisms of acute gout treatment and long-term urate-lowering therapy.
back:
• Acute: Anti-inflammatory (NSAIDs, Colchicine, Steroids); no effect on urate levels.
• Long-term: Urate-lowering (Allopurinol, Probenecid); prevents crystal deposition.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: How does lactic acidosis secondary to heavy alcohol consumption exacerbate an acute gouty attack?
back:
• Lactate and urate share the same renal transporter.
• Elevated lactate competitively inhibits urate excretion in the kidney.
• This leads to worsened hyperuricemia.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Identify the primary source of excess uric acid in patients with Von Gierke disease (Glucose 6-Phosphatase deficiency).
back:
• Glucose 6-phosphate accumulates and enters the HMP shunt.
• This increases Ribose 5-phosphate and PRPP levels.
• Overproduction of PRPP accelerates de novo purine synthesis and degradation.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Definitive diagnosis of gout via synovial fluid aspiration reveals [___] shaped crystals that show negative birefringence under polarized light.
back:
• Needle-shaped monosodium urate.
• Indicates an acute inflammatory response.
• Differentiates gout from pseudogout (rhomboid-shaped).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 6-month-old infant presents with recurrent pneumonia, chronic diarrhea, and persistent oral candidiasis. Laboratory tests reveal a profound lack of T, B, and NK cells. Identify the likely enzyme deficiency.
back:
• Adenosine Deaminase (ADA).
• Causes Autosomal Recessive SCID.
• Leads to lymphocytopenia via dATP toxicity.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain the role of deoxyadenosine triphosphate (dATP) accumulation in the pathogenesis of SCID.
back:
• High dATP inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase.
• Prevents synthesis of all deoxyribonucleotides.
• Blocks DNA replication and lymphocyte division.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Distinguish between Primary Hyperuricemia caused by PRPP Synthetase mutation versus Secondary Hyperuricemia caused by von Gierke disease.
back:
• Primary: X-linked mutation increases Vmax for PRPP production.
• Secondary: G6P accumulation drives Pentose Phosphate Pathway.
• Both result in excess PRPP driving purine overproduction.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Describe the biochemical mechanism by which Allopurinol lowers serum uric acid levels.
back:
• Structural analog of hypoxanthine.
• Competitively inhibits Xanthine Oxidase.
• Increases more-soluble hypoxanthine and xanthine excretion.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: The nodular masses formed by the deposition of monosodium urate crystals in soft tissues, such as the ear helix or Achilles tendon, are called [___].
back:
• Tophi (singular: Tophus).
• Characteristic of chronic tophaceous gout.
• Indicates long-standing, poorly controlled hyperuricemia.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 50-year-old male with chronic alcoholism presents with acute big toe pain (podagra). Biochemistry shows elevated serum urate and lactate. Explain the renal interaction causing this presentation.
back:
• Lactic acidosis induces competition.
• Lactate and urate compete for same renal transporters.
• Decreased urate excretion triggers hyperuricemia.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the immunological cellular profiles of Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency and Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency.
back:
• ADA: Depletes T, B, and NK cells (severe SCID).
• PNP: Affects T-cells primarily.
• Both result in recurrent infections.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Distinguish the clinical indication for Probenecid versus Allopurinol in gout management.
back:
• Probenecid: Uricosuric agent for 'underexcretors' (increases renal loss).
• Allopurinol: Synthesis inhibitor for 'overproducers' (blocks XO).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Identify the primary source of nitrogen and carbon atoms for the pyrimidine ring that is also shared by the purine synthesis pathway.
back:
• Glutamine and Aspartic Acid.
• Both pathways require PRPP as well.
• Essential for nitrogen donation.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: In the diagnosis of gout, synovial fluid analysis under polarized light microscopy typically reveals needle-shaped crystals showing [___] birefringence.
back:
• Negative birefringence.
• Crystals are needle-shaped monosodium urate.
• Often found within polymorphonuclear leukocytes during acute inflammatory flares in the synovial fluid.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: An 8-month-old infant presents with recurrent pneumonia, chronic diarrhea, and persistent oral candidiasis. Lab data shows a near-total absence of T, B, and NK cells. Identify the likely enzyme deficiency.
back:
• Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency.
• Results in Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID).
• Characterized by profound lymphocytopenia affecting T, B, and NK cells, leading to early death if untreated.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency leads to the inhibition of DNA synthesis in lymphocytes.
back:
• Accumulation of dATP occurs.
• dATP allosterically inhibits ribonucleotide reductase.
• This prevents the synthesis of deoxyribonucleotides, thus halting DNA replication and lymphocyte proliferation in the bone marrow.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the biochemical etiology of gout caused by Von Gierke disease versus that caused by Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
back:
• Von Gierke: G6P accumulation increases HMP shunt activity, providing excess PRPP.
• Lesch-Nyhan: HGPRT deficiency fails to salvage bases, causing both PRPP accumulation and increased de novo purine synthesis.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Identify the specific enzyme inhibited by Allopurinol and the resulting metabolic intermediates that accumulate because they are more water-soluble than uric acid.
back:
• Enzyme: Xanthine Oxidase.
• Accumulated Intermediates: Hypoxanthine and Xanthine.
• These compounds are more water-soluble than uric acid, reducing crystal deposition and inflammatory joint response.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency is inherited as an [___] disorder and represents a significant percentage of all SCID cases.
back:
• Autosomal recessive.
• Represents roughly 14% of SCID cases.
• Clinical presentation involves "bubble boy" susceptibility to pneumonia and chronic diarrhea due to lack of functional immune cells.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A patient with a history of painful joint swelling in the great toe starts a high-protein diet (meat/seafood) and develops a flare-up. Explain the relationship between diet and the end-product of this metabolic pathway.
back:
• Diet provides purines that are degraded to uric acid in the intestinal mucosa.
• Humans lack urate oxidase, making uric acid the relatively insoluble end-product.
• Excessive levels precipitate as monosodium urate.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Describe how lactic acidosis or the use of thiazide diuretics can trigger a secondary gout attack.
back:
• Lactate and thiazides compete with urate for common renal secretory transporters.
• This competition decreases the renal excretion of uric acid.
• The resulting hyperuricemia facilitates the precipitation of monosodium urate crystals.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Distinguish between Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency and Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency regarding cell-type specificity.
back:
• ADA Deficiency: Causes total lymphocytopenia (T, B, and NK cells).
• PNP Deficiency: Primarily affects T-cells; B-cell function is usually maintained.
• PNP is generally less severe than ADA-SCID.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Name the nodular masses of monosodium urate crystals that deposit in soft tissues during chronic gout and identify their typical clinical appearance.
back:
• Tophi.
• Appear as hard, chalky, or white nodular masses.
• Commonly deposited in the olecranon bursa, Achilles tendon, or ear helix during the chronic stage of tophaceous gout.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: The definitive diagnosis of gout requires the identification of needle-shaped, negatively birefringent [___] crystals in synovial fluid.
back:
• Monosodium urate.
• Found within polymorphonuclear leukocytes.
• Triggers intense inflammatory response in joints.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 6-month-old infant presents with recurrent pneumonia, chronic diarrhea, and persistent thrush. Labs show profound lymphocytopenia. Name the most likely enzyme deficiency related to purine catabolism.
back:
• Adenosine Deaminase (ADA).
• Causes Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID).
• Affects T, B, and Natural Killer (NK) cells.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain how a deficiency in Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) leads to the failure of DNA synthesis in lymphocytes.
back:
• ADA deficiency causes accumulation of dATP.
• High dATP inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase.
• Prevents production of all deoxyribonucleotides.
• Halts DNA replication and cell division.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A patient with von Gierke disease presents with swollen, painful joints. Contrast the mechanism of hyperuricemia in this patient with primary underexcretion gout.
back:
• Von Gierke: Lactic acidosis competes for renal urate excretion.
• Primary Gout: Inherent renal transporter defect (90% of cases).
• Both lead to decreased renal clearance of uric acid.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Describe the pharmacological action of Allopurinol in the long-term management of chronic gout.
back:
• Structural analog of hypoxanthine.
• Suicide inhibitor of Xanthine Oxidase.
• Lowers uric acid levels.
• Increases more soluble precursors (Xanthine/Hypoxanthine).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Nodular masses formed by the deposition of monosodium urate crystals in soft tissues, such as the ear or joints, are termed [___].
back:
• Tophi.
• Characteristic of chronic tophaceous gout.
• Indicates long-term uncontrolled hyperuricemia.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A man experiences sudden, excruciating pain in his big toe after a seafood dinner and alcohol. What is the metabolic basis for alcohol-induced gouty flares?
back:
• Alcohol increases lactate production.
• Lactate inhibits renal urate excretion.
• Seafood provides high purine load for degradation.
• Rapid rise in serum urate triggers crystallization.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Identify the biological distinction between Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency and Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency regarding immune cell impact.
back:
• ADA deficiency: Depletes T, B, and NK cells.
• PNP deficiency: Primarily affects T-cells.
• ADA causes severe lymphocytopenia; PNP is less severe.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the metabolic end products of purine degradation in humans with those of pyrimidine degradation.
back:
• Purines: Uric acid (poorly soluble; triggers inflammation).
• Pyrimidines: Beta-alanine and Beta-aminoisobutyrate.
• Pyrimidine products are highly soluble and non-toxic.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: State the primary cellular target of Colchicine in the treatment of acute gout.
back:
• Inhibits microtubule polymerization.
• Prevents neutrophil migration (chemotaxis) to joints.
• Does not affect uric acid levels.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: In the management of chronic gout, the drug allopurinol effectively lowers plasma urate levels by inhibiting the enzyme [___].
back:
• Xanthine Oxidase (XO)
• Blocks conversion of hypoxanthine/xanthine to uric acid
• Leads to accumulation of more soluble precursors

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 6-month-old infant presents with recurrent severe infections and failure to thrive. Laboratory data reveals a profound depletion of T, B, and NK cells. Name the most likely enzymatic deficiency.
back:
• Adenosine Deaminase (ADA)
• Results in Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID)
• Characterized by lymphocytopenia and developmental arrest

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain why elevated levels of deoxyadenosine triphosphate (dATP) lead to immunodeficiency in ADA-deficient patients.
back:
• Allosterically inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase
• Prevents synthesis of all deoxyribonucleotides (dNTPs)
• Halts DNA replication and cell division
• Triggers apoptosis in lymphocytes

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the cell types affected in Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency versus Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency.
back:
• ADA: Depletes T-cells, B-cells, and NK-cells (Full SCID)
• PNP: Primarily affects T-cells
• ADA is significantly more severe and frequent

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Describe the characteristic appearance of joint aspirate crystals under polarized light microscopy that confirms a diagnosis of gout.
back:
• Needle-shaped
• Negatively birefringent
• Monosodium urate (MSU) crystals

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: The primary enzyme responsible for the hydrolytic removal of the amino group from adenosine to produce inosine is [___].
back:
• Adenosine Deaminase (ADA)
• Essential for purine degradation
• Deficiency causes metabolite accumulation toxic to lymphocytes

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A patient undergoing chemotherapy for leukemia suddenly develops acute pain and swelling in the big toe. Identify the metabolic byproduct responsible.
back:
• Uric Acid (Urate)
• Caused by massive purine degradation from cell turnover
• Leads to secondary hyperuricemia and acute gouty arthritis

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: How does Colchicine provide relief during an acute gouty attack without affecting systemic uric acid levels?
back:
• Inhibits microtubule polymerization
• Prevents neutrophil migration to the joint
• Suppresses the inflammatory response to urate crystals

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Distinguish between 'underexcretion' and 'overproduction' as causes of hyperuricemia in the majority of gout patients.
back:
• Underexcretion: Primary cause (>90%), involves renal defects or diuretics
• Overproduction: Less common, involves PRPP synthetase mutations or cell turnover

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: State the biochemical reason why lactic acidosis can precipitate an acute episode of gout.
back:
• Competition for renal transporters
• Lactate and urate use same transporters in the kidney
• Increased lactate decreases urate excretion, raising plasma levels

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: The end product of purine catabolism in humans that precipitates as monosodium urate crystals in joints is [___].
back:
• Uric acid
• Produced primarily in the liver
• Final product of xanthine oxidation

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 55-year-old male presents with sudden, excruciating pain in the first metatarsophalangeal joint. Aspiration shows needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals. What is the diagnosis?
back:
• Acute Gouty Arthritis (Podagra)
• Caused by monosodium urate deposition
• Associated with hyperuricemia

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain the role of dATP accumulation in the pathophysiology of Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency.
back:
• ADA deficiency increases dATP levels
• dATP strongly inhibits ribonucleotide reductase
• This halts DNA synthesis, leading to T and B cell apoptosis

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the typical joint fluid findings of Gout with Pseudogout under polarized light microscopy.
back:
• Gout: Needle-shaped; Negatively birefringent (Yellow when parallel)
• Pseudogout: Rhomboid-shaped; Positively birefringent (Blue when parallel)
• Gout involves urate; Pseudogout involves calcium pyrophosphate

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Identify the pharmacological target of Allopurinol and its mechanism for treating chronic gout.
back:
• Enzyme: Xanthine Oxidase
• Mechanism: Suicide inhibition (via oxypurinol)
• Result: Decreased production of uric acid

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: In the laboratory diagnosis of SCID due to ADA deficiency, the defining hematological finding is severe [___].
back:
• Lymphocytopenia
• Depletion of T, B, and NK cells
• Resulting in profound immunodeficiency

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 4-month-old infant presents with recurrent pneumonia, oral candidiasis, and an absent thymic shadow on X-ray. Genetic testing reveals an autosomal recessive enzyme defect. Name the likely enzyme.
back:
• Adenosine Deaminase (ADA)
• Causes 14% of SCID cases
• Autosomal recessive inheritance

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Describe why hyperlactatemia (e.g., in von Gierke disease or strenuous exercise) can trigger a gouty attack.
back:
• Lactate and urate compete for the same renal transporters
• High lactate levels inhibit renal urate excretion
• Results in secondary hyperuricemia

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Distinguish between the primary metabolic causes of 'Underexcretion' vs 'Overproduction' in hyperuricemia.
back:
• Underexcretion (90%): Renal handling defects or competition with organic acids
• Overproduction (10%): Increased PRPP synthetase activity or high cell turnover (cancer)

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: State the typical pH-related solubility characteristic of uric acid in the renal tubules.
back:
• Uric acid is less soluble at acidic pH
• Acidic urine (pH < 5.5) promotes crystal formation
• Predisposes to urolithiasis (kidney stones)

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: In the definitive diagnosis of Gout, aspirated synovial fluid under polarized light microscopy reveals needle-shaped [___] crystals.
back: Monosodium urate (MSU) crystals (exhibiting strong negative birefringence).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 6-month-old infant presents with recurrent pneumonia, chronic diarrhea, and persistent oral candidiasis. Labs show a profound decrease in T, B, and NK cells. Identify the likely enzyme deficiency.
back: Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency (causing Severe Combined Immunodeficiency - SCID).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency causes developmental arrest and apoptosis in lymphocytes.
back: Accumulation of dATP allosterically inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase, preventing the synthesis of all other deoxyribonucleotides (dNDPs) required for DNA replication.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the polarized light microscopic appearance of Gout crystals with those of Calcium Pyrophosphate Deposition Disease (Pseudogout).
back: Gout: Needle-shaped and negatively birefringent (yellow when parallel to axis). Pseudogout: Rhomboid-shaped and positively birefringent (blue when parallel to axis).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Name the specific enzyme inhibited by Allopurinol and identify the more water-soluble purine metabolites that accumulate as a result.
back: Enzyme: Xanthine Oxidase. Accumulating metabolites: Hypoxanthine and Xanthine.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: An X-linked recessive mutation resulting in a virtually complete deficiency of [___] leads to Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, presenting with hyperuricemia and choreoathetosis.
back: Hypoxanthine-Guanine Phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A patient with leukemia undergoing chemotherapy develops acute podagra. Explain the link between cell turnover and this arthritic presentation.
back: Secondary hyperuricemia caused by massive purine release from dying tumor cells (Tumor Lysis Syndrome), leading to MSU crystal deposition.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Describe how Glucose-6-Phosphatase deficiency (Von Gierke Disease) contributes to the development of gouty arthritis.
back: Increased G6P is shunted into the Pentose Phosphate Pathway, elevating Ribose-5-Phosphate and PRPP production, which drives de novo purine synthesis and subsequent uric acid degradation.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Distinguish between the primary cause of Gout in 90% of patients versus the mechanism seen in patients with PRPP Synthetase overactivity.
back: 90% of patients: Renal underexcretion of uric acid. PRPP Synthetase overactivity: Overproduction of purines (increased Vmax or decreased inhibition).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: List the three definitive therapeutic interventions for a child diagnosed with SCID due to ADA deficiency.
back: 1. Bone Marrow Transplantation (BMT). 2. Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT). 3. Gene Therapy.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: The final metabolic end product of purine catabolism in humans, which precipitates as monosodium urate in joints, is [___].
back: - Uric acid; - Relatively insoluble molecule; - Formed from xanthine by xanthine oxidase.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 50-year-old male presents with sudden, excruciating pain and swelling of the first metatarsophalangeal joint. Identify the likely diagnosis and the microscopic appearance of the culprit crystals.
back: - Diagnosis: Gout (Podagra); - Appearance: Needle-shaped crystals; - Polarized light: Strongly negatively birefringent.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain the role of accumulated dATP in the pathophysiology of Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency regarding DNA synthesis.
back: - dATP inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase; - Prevents production of all deoxyribonucleotides (dNTPs); - Arrests DNA replication and lymphocyte division.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the pharmacological targets for a gouty patient classified as an 'underexcretor' versus an 'overproducer' of urate.
back: - Underexcretors: Target renal excretion using Uricosuric agents (e.g., Probenecid); - Overproducers: Target synthesis using Xanthine Oxidase inhibitors (e.g., Allopurinol).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Describe the mechanism of action of Colchicine during an acute gouty flare, specifically regarding leukocyte function.
back: - Binds to tubulin to inhibit microtubule polymerization; - Decreases neutrophil migration into the affected joint; - Reduces inflammatory response to urate crystals.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency follows an [___] inheritance pattern and results in a severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID).
back: - Autosomal recessive; - Causes T, B, and NK cell depletion; - Leads to early childhood mortality from infections.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A patient with chronic alcoholism presents with hyperuricemia. Laboratory data reveals elevated serum lactate. Explain why lactic acidosis induces this condition.
back: - Lactate competes with urate for renal transporters; - Decreased renal clearance of uric acid; - Results in secondary hyperuricemia and gout.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 6-month-old infant presents with recurrent pneumonia, persistent oral thrush, and lymphopenia. Link these laboratory and clinical findings to a specific purine enzyme defect.
back: - Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency; - Lymphotoxicity from dATP accumulation; - Causes Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Differentiate the solubility and metabolic fate of xanthine versus uric acid in a patient treated with Allopurinol.
back: - Xanthine/Hypoxanthine: High solubility, easily excreted in urine; - Uric Acid: Low solubility, precipitates in joints as urate.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Identify the term for the characteristic nodular masses of monosodium urate crystals deposited in soft tissues during chronic gout.
back: - Tophi (Tophus); - Associated with chronic tophaceous gout; - Commonly found in the ear helix or joints.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: In Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency, the toxic intracellular accumulation of [___] directly inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, halting DNA synthesis in lymphocytes.
back: • dATP (deoxyadenosine triphosphate). • Leads to developmental arrest and apoptosis. • Affects T, B, and NK cells.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 52-year-old male presents with excruciating pain in the big toe. Polarized light microscopy of synovial fluid shows needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals. Identify the diagnosis.
back: • Acute Gouty Arthritis. • Caused by monosodium urate crystal deposition. • Triggers an acute inflammatory response.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain the biochemical consequence of elevated dATP levels on the S-phase of the cell cycle in SCID patients.
back: • Inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase. • Prevents production of all deoxyribonucleotides (dNTPs). • Effectively stops DNA replication and cell division.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 4-month-old infant with recurrent fungal infections and failure to thrive shows a lack of thymic shadow on X-ray and absolute lymphopenia. Contrast the inheritance of the most common ADA-related SCID with X-linked SCID.
back: • ADA deficiency: Autosomal Recessive. • X-linked SCID: IL-2 receptor gamma chain mutation. • ADA affects T, B, and NK cells.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Name the structural analog of hypoxanthine used for long-term gout management and specify its mechanism regarding Xanthine Oxidase.
back: • Allopurinol. • Suicide (irreversible) inhibition. • Converted to oxypurinol, which binds the enzyme active site.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: The characteristic nodular masses of monosodium urate crystals deposited in the ear helix or joints of patients with chronic hyperuricemia are called [___].
back: • Tophi. • Indicate chronic tophaceous gout. • Result from prolonged urate saturation.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A patient with von Gierke disease (G6Pase deficiency) develops painful joint swelling. How does this metabolic defect lead to secondary hyperuricemia?
back: • Diverts G6P to HMP shunt, increasing PRPP synthesis. • Lactic acidosis competes with urate for renal excretion. • Result: Overproduction and underexcretion of uric acid.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Describe the mechanism by which Colchicine provides relief during an acute gouty attack despite having no effect on uric acid levels.
back: • Inhibits microtubule polymerization by binding tubulin. • Prevents neutrophil migration to the joint. • Suppresses the inflammatory response to urate crystals.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Distinguish between the primary cause of hyperuricemia in the majority of gout patients versus those with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
back: • Majority (~90%): Underexcretion (renal defects). • Lesch-Nyhan: Overproduction (HGPRT deficiency/PRPP buildup).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Identify the definitive gold-standard investigation required to confirm a diagnosis of Gout.
back: • Arthrocentesis (Joint fluid aspiration). • Examination under polarized light microscopy. • Identification of monosodium urate crystals.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Definitive diagnosis of gouty arthritis is established by identifying [___] crystals within aspirated synovial fluid.
back:
• Monosodium urate crystals.
• Appearance: Needle-shaped.
• Polarized light: Strongly negative birefringence.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 4-month-old infant presents with lymphocytopenia and recurrent severe infections. Laboratory data reveals significantly elevated dATP levels in red blood cells. Identify the enzyme deficiency.
back:
• Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency.
• Inherited as autosomal recessive.
• Leads to Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism through which elevated intracellular dATP causes immune cell death in ADA deficiency.
back:
• dATP inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase.
• Prevents production of all deoxyribonucleotides.
• Blocks DNA synthesis and cell division.
• Triggers apoptosis in T, B, and NK cells.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the pharmacological mechanisms of Allopurinol versus Probenecid in managing chronic gout.
back:
• Allopurinol: Inhibits Xanthine Oxidase (reduces production).
• Probenecid: Uricosuric agent (blocks renal reabsorption).
• Probenecid is specific for 'underexcretors' with normal renal function.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Specify the metabolic consequence of gain-of-function mutations in X-linked PRPP synthetase.
back:
• Increased Vmax or decreased sensitivity to inhibitors.
• Excessive production of PRPP.
• Overproduction of purines leading to hyperuricemia and Gout.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: The characteristic nodular masses of monosodium urate crystals deposited in the soft tissues of chronic gout patients are termed [___].
back:
• Tophi (Tophaceous Gout).
• Occur in ears, joints, or pressure points.
• Represent advanced, poorly controlled hyperuricemia.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A patient with an acute gouty flare is prescribed Colchicine. Describe how this drug alleviates joint inflammation without affecting uric acid levels.
back:
• Inhibits microtubule assembly.
• Prevents neutrophil migration into the joint.
• Only treats inflammation; does not reduce hyperuricemia.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Analyze why lactic acidosis can precipitate or worsen a gouty attack.
back:
• Lactate competes with urate for renal transporters.
• High serum lactate reduces renal urate excretion.
• Causes secondary hyperuricemia (underexcretion type).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Distinguish between ADA deficiency and Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency based on cell type involvement.
back:
• ADA: Affects T-cells, B-cells, and NK-cells (SCID).
• PNP: Primarily affects T-cells (milder immunodeficiency).
• Both are autosomal recessive disorders.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: State the standard therapeutic options for children diagnosed with Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID) due to ADA deficiency.
back:
• Bone Marrow Transplantation (BMT).
• Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT).
• Gene Therapy.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: The definitive diagnosis of gout is confirmed by identifying [___] crystals in synovial fluid using polarized light microscopy.
back:
• Monosodium urate crystals.
• Appear as needle-shaped structures.
• Exhibit strong negative birefringence.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 6-month-old infant presents with recurrent pneumonia, chronic diarrhea, and absent thymic shadow. Lab data reveals extreme lymphopenia and elevated dATP. Identify the enzyme deficiency.
back:
• Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency.
• Causes Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID).
• Results in depletion of T, B, and NK cells.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain the biochemical role of Ribonucleotide Reductase inhibition in the pathogenesis of ADA-deficient SCID.
back:
• Accumulation of dATP allosterically inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase.
• This prevents the synthesis of all other deoxyribonucleotides.
• DNA replication and lymphocyte division are halted.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the clinical laboratory findings of Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency with those of Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency.
back:
• ADA Deficiency: Depletes T, B, and NK cells (severe SCID).
• PNP Deficiency: Primarily affects T-cells (milder, though still severe).
• Both present with recurrent infections.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Describe the metabolic transformation and inhibitory action of Allopurinol in managing chronic gout.
back:
• Converted by xanthine oxidase to oxypurinol (alloxanthine).
• Acts as a suicide inhibitor of Xanthine Oxidase.
• Reduces uric acid production by stopping hypoxanthine/xanthine oxidation.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Nodular masses of monosodium urate crystals deposited in soft tissues such as the Achilles tendon or ear helix are termed [___].
back:
• Tophi.
• Characteristic of chronic tophaceous gout.
• Usually develop after years of untreated hyperuricemia.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A leukemia patient undergoing chemotherapy suddenly develops intense pain and swelling in the first metatarsophalangeal joint. Explain the biochemical cause of this acute data point.
back:
• Secondary hyperuricemia due to Tumor Lysis Syndrome.
• Rapid cell breakdown increases purine release.
• Excessive degradation results in uric acid levels exceeding saturation.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain how von Gierke disease (Type I GSD) mechanistically contributes to the development of gout.
back:
• G6P accumulation drives the Pentose Phosphate Pathway.
• This increases PRPP synthesis, accelerating de novo purine production.
• Elevated lactate competes with urate for renal excretion.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast 'underexcretors' and 'overproducers' as the two primary metabolic drivers of hyperuricemia in gout.
back:
• Underexcretors (90%): Renal handling defects; worsened by diuretics or lead.
• Overproducers (10%): Idiopathic, PRPP synthetase mutations, or high cell turnover.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Name the two primary standard definitive treatments for ADA-deficient SCID that address the underlying genetic/enzymatic lack.
back:
• Bone Marrow Transplantation (BMT).
• Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT).
• Gene Therapy is also a clinical option.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: Hereditary orotic aciduria is caused by a deficiency in the bifunctional enzyme [___], which possesses both orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and orotidylate decarboxylase activities.
back:
• UMP Synthase
• Required for de novo pyrimidine synthesis
• Converts orotic acid into UMP

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: A 10-month-old infant presents with megaloblastic anemia and failure to thrive. Lab tests show high urinary orotic acid but normal ammonia levels. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Hereditary Orotic Aciduria
• Caused by UMP Synthase defect
• Anemia is unresponsive to Vitamin B12 or Folate

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: Explain the biochemical rationale for administering oral uridine to patients with hereditary orotic aciduria.
back:
• Uridine is salvaged to UMP via nucleoside kinases
• Bypasses the metabolic block at UMP Synthase
• Provides feedback inhibition of CPS-II to reduce orotate production

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: Contrast the laboratory findings of Orotic Aciduria caused by UMP Synthase deficiency versus Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency.
back:
• UMP Synthase: Normal blood ammonia; megaloblastic anemia present
• OTC Deficiency: Hyperammonemia present; megaloblastic anemia absent
• Both: Elevated urinary orotic acid

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: Describe how a defect in the urea cycle enzyme Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) leads to increased pyrimidine synthesis.
back:
• Carbamoyl phosphate accumulates in mitochondria
• Excess leaks into the cytosol
• Stimulates de novo pyrimidine synthesis by bypassing the regulated CPS-II step

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: In the de novo pyrimidine synthesis pathway, the enzyme [___] is the primary regulated step and is inhibited by UTP.
back:
• Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS-II)
• Located in the cytosol
• Activated by PRPP

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: A male neonate presents with lethargy and seizures. Lab work reveals severe hyperammonemia and high orotic acid levels in the urine. Identify the deficient enzyme.
back:
• Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC)
• Most common urea cycle disorder
• X-linked inheritance pattern

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: Explain why a deficiency in UMP Synthase leads to megaloblastic anemia despite adequate Folate and B12 levels.
back:
• Leads to pyrimidine deficiency (CTP, TTP)
• Causes inadequate substrates for DNA synthesis
• Results in asynchronous nuclear/cytoplasmic maturation in erythrocytes

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: Distinguish between Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I and II regarding their cellular location and nitrogen source.
back:
• CPS-I: Mitochondria; uses Ammonia (Urea Cycle)
• CPS-II: Cytosol; uses Glutamine (Pyrimidine Synthesis)

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: Name the mitochondrial enzyme in the pyrimidine pathway that produces orotic acid and identify its unique location.
back:
• Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase
• Located on the inner mitochondrial membrane
• All other de novo pyrimidine enzymes are cytosolic

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
coreConcept: Uric Acid as Purine End Product
front: In the metabolic breakdown of purines, the relatively insoluble end product that accumulates in the blood of patients with Gout is [___].
back:
• Uric acid
• Produced from hypoxanthine and xanthine via xanthine oxidase
• Excess levels lead to monosodium urate crystal deposition.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: A 52-year-old male presents with sudden, nocturnal, excruciating pain and erythema at the base of his big toe. Arthrocentesis is performed; identify the most likely microscopic finding.
back:
• Needle-shaped crystals
• Negatively birefringent under polarized light
• Monosodium urate (MSU) composition
• Diagnostic of Podagra (Acute Gout).

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism behind lymphotoxicity in Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency.
back:
• ADA deficiency causes accumulation of Adenosine/Deoxyadenosine.
• These are converted to high levels of dATP.
• Elevated dATP inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase.
• Resulting DNA synthesis failure leads to T and B cell depletion.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the primary renal mechanism of action for Probenecid versus Allopurinol in gout management.
back:
• Allopurinol: Inhibits xanthine oxidase; reduces systemic uric acid production.
• Probenecid: Uricosuric agent; inhibits proximal tubule reabsorption of urate.
• Allopurinol is for overproducers; Probenecid for underexcretors.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Name the specific metabolic condition where rapid cell turnover during chemotherapy leads to secondary hyperuricemia and potential renal failure.
back:
• Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS)
• Massive release of intracellular purines occurs.
• Rapid catabolism exceeds renal clearance of uric acid.
• Managed with aggressive hydration and Rasburicase/Allopurinol.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency is an autosomal [___] disorder that is a leading cause of Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID).
back:
• Recessive
• Characterized by failure to thrive and recurrent infections
• Accounts for approximately 14% of SCID cases in the US.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: An infant presents with chronic diarrhea, persistent oral thrush, and multiple episodes of pneumonia. Lab data shows a 'near zero' lymphocyte count. Identify the suspected diagnosis and the primary treatment.
back:
• Diagnosis: SCID (likely ADA deficiency)
• Treatment: Bone marrow (Stem Cell) transplantation
• Alternative: Enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) or Gene therapy.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: How does the administration of Colchicine provide relief during an acute gouty flare without altering plasma urate levels?
back:
• Binds to tubulin and inhibits microtubule polymerization.
• Impairs neutrophil chemotaxis and migration to the joint.
• Suppresses the inflammatory response to urate crystals.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Contrast the metabolic triggers and renal competition involved in alcohol-induced gouty attacks.
back:
• Alcohol metabolism increases Lactic Acid production.
• Lactate competes with Urate for renal excretion sites.
• Urate is retained, triggering hyperuricemia and flares.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
front: Identify the characteristic physical exam finding in chronic gout consisting of non-tender, chalky-white nodular deposits.
back:
• Tophi (Tophaceous Gout)
• Located in soft tissues, ear helix, or Achilles tendons
• Represent large aggregates of urate crystals and granulomatous inflammation.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: The bifunctional cytosolic enzyme, whose deficiency leads to hereditary orotic aciduria and megaloblastic anemia, is [___].
back:
UMP Synthase.
• It possesses Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase activities.
• Converts orotate into UMP using PRPP as a ribose donor.
• Essential for de novo pyrimidine synthesis.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: A 1-year-old infant presents with failure to thrive and megaloblastic anemia unresponsive to Vitamin B12 or folate. Lab tests reveal high urinary orotate. Name the diagnosis.
back:
Hereditary Orotic Aciduria.
• Caused by autosomal recessive deficiency of UMP synthase.
• Results in pyrimidine starvation.
• Leads to impaired DNA synthesis and erythropoiesis.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: Explain the therapeutic mechanism of oral uridine administration in patients with UMP synthase deficiency.
back:
Uridine acts as a salvage source.
• Phosphorylated to UMP via nucleoside kinases.
• Bypasses the enzymatic block in the de novo pathway.
• Provides necessary pyrimidines for DNA/RNA production.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: Distinguish between the orotic aciduria seen in UMP synthase deficiency and that seen in Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency regarding laboratory findings.
back:
UMP Synthase Deficiency: Normal ammonia, megaloblastic anemia present.
• OTC Deficiency: High blood ammonia (hyperammonemia), no megaloblastic anemia.
• OTC deficiency causes mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate to spill into the cytosol.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: Identify the metabolic 'spillover' mechanism that causes secondary orotic aciduria in certain urea cycle defects.
back:
Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency.
• Mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate accumulates and enters the cytosol.
• Bypasses the regulated CPS-II step.
• Excess substrate drives uncontrolled orotic acid production via the pyrimidine pathway.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: The rate-limiting and regulated step of pyrimidine biosynthesis in mammalian cells is catalyzed by the cytosolic enzyme [___].
back:
Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II).
• Allosterically inhibited by UTP (end-product).
• Allosterically activated by PRPP.
• Uses Glutamine as the nitrogen donor.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: A child with poor growth and high urinary orotic acid shows normal serum ammonia levels. Explain the clinical significance of the normal ammonia level.
back:
It excludes Urea Cycle Defects.
• High orotic acid with normal ammonia confirms Hereditary Orotic Aciduria (UMP Synthase deficiency).
• High orotic acid with high ammonia indicates OTC deficiency.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: Explain why megaloblastic anemia occurs specifically in hereditary orotic aciduria but not typically in OTC deficiency.
back:
Hereditary form causes total pyrimidine deficiency.
• Lack of dTMP and dCTP prevents DNA replication in bone marrow.
• In OTC deficiency, the pyrimidine pathway is hyperactive, so nucleotides are abundant.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: Contrast Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I and II regarding their cellular location and metabolic pathways.
back:
CPS I: Mitochondrial; Urea Cycle; uses NH3 nitrogen; activated by N-acetylglutamate.
• CPS II: Cytosolic; Pyrimidine synthesis; uses Glutamine nitrogen; activated by PRPP.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: List the three specific precursors that contribute atoms directly to the formation of the pyrimidine ring before PRPP is added.
back:
Glutamine (Nitrogen).
• Aspartic Acid (Nitrogen and Carbons).
• CO2 (Carbon).
• Note: These form the initial ring; ribose-phosphate is added later.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: The bifunctional enzyme [___] is deficient in hereditary orotic aciduria, which catalyzes the final two steps of the de novo pyrimidine synthesis pathway.
back:
UMP Synthase.

*   Includes orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and orotidylate decarboxylase activities.
*   Deficiency leads to orotic acid buildup and pyrimidine starvation.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
coreConcept: Clinical Presentation of Hereditary Orotic Aciduria
front: A 14-month-old child presents with megaloblastic anemia, failure to thrive, and white crystals in the diaper. Lab results show normal blood ammonia levels. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
Hereditary Orotic Aciduria.

*   Anemia is refractory to Vitamin B12 and Folate.
*   Differentiated from OTC deficiency by the absence of hyperammonemia.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism that links a deficiency in the urea cycle enzyme Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) to the development of orotic aciduria.
back:
*   OTC deficiency causes carbamoyl phosphate to accumulate in the mitochondria.
*   Excess carbamoyl phosphate leaks into the cytosol.
*   It enters the pyrimidine pathway, bypassing the rate-limiting CPS-II step.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
coreConcept: Differential Diagnosis: OTC vs. UMP Synthase Deficiency
front: A male neonate presents with lethargy, vomiting, and high serum ammonia. Urine analysis reveals elevated orotic acid. Contrast the pathophysiology of this case with hereditary orotic aciduria regarding the urea cycle.
back:
*   This case: OTC deficiency (Urea Cycle defect) causes hyperammonemia.
*   Hereditary Orotic Aciduria: UMP synthase defect; no hyperammonemia; presents with megaloblastic anemia.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea

* This drives excessive, unregulated production of orotic acid.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
front: In the de novo pyrimidine synthesis pathway, the rate-limiting cytosolic enzyme regulated by UTP and PRPP is [___].

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
